scenario: 演唱会开票瞬间，Ticketmaster 上万人同时点向同一个座位 A15。
q: Contention 在系统设计里指什么？
options: 多个进程同时争抢同一份资源，比如最后一张票或同一个拍卖品
系统里只有读请求，完全没有任何写请求会发生
数据库表里只存放几乎从不会发生变化的静态配置选项，几乎没有并发写
各个微服务彼此之间完全没有共享状态或共享数据
options_en: Multiple processes competing for the same resource at the same time, like the last concert ticket or one auction item.
The system only ever receives read requests and never any writes at all.
The database table only stores static configuration that almost never changes, with almost no concurrent writes at all.
Different microservices share no state or data with each other at all, ever.
why: Contention 是多个并发操作争抢同一资源。不协调就会出现 race condition、重复预订、重复扣款或状态不一致。
why_en: Contention happens when multiple processes compete for the same resource at the same time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个进程/请求同时争抢同一份资源或同一行数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contention means multiple processes compete for the same resource at the same time.

q_en: What does contention mean in system design?
optionExplanations: 这就是 contention 的定义——谁先谁后决定结果，需要协调机制介入。
纯读流量各自独立返回，不存在互相覆盖的写入，谈不上 contention。
配置几乎不变意味着极少并发写，天然没有竞态窗口。
服务之间没有共享状态就没有共同争抢的资源，自然不会有 contention。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly contention—timing decides the outcome, so you need coordination.
Read-only traffic returns independently with nothing being overwritten, so there is no contention.
Static config barely changes, so there is almost no concurrent write to race over.
With no shared state between services there is no common resource to fight over.
scenario_en: The instant tickets drop on Ticketmaster, tens of thousands of people tap the same seat A15 at once.

scenario: 抢票服务里两个请求同时读到 available_seats=1，各自在应用代码里减一后写回。
q: Lost update 的本质是什么？
options: 两个请求读到同一个旧值，各自写回导致后写覆盖了先写的结果
数据库所在磁盘出现物理损坏，导致这批数据永久丢失
缓存条目 TTL 设置太短，读请求频繁 miss 后要回源
用户在提交表单前离开了页面，请求根本没有发出
options_en: Two requests read the same old value, both write back, and the later write silently overwrites the earlier one's result.
The database's underlying disk suffers physical damage and this batch of data is permanently lost.
The cache entry's TTL is set too short, so reads miss frequently and have to fall back to the source.
The user left the page before submitting the form, so the request was never sent.
why: Lost update 是 read-modify-write 周期里的经典竞态：读和写不是一个原子动作，中间状态可能被别人改变。
why_en: A lost update occurs when concurrent read-modify-write cycles act on the same stale value and one write silently overwrites another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并发的 read-modify-write 导致一次更新被另一次悄悄覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update happens when one concurrent write silently overwrites another transaction's change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读取当前值，再基于它计算结果并写回的操作序列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-modify-write means reading a value, computing a change, then writing it back.

q_en: What is the core problem in a lost update?
optionExplanations: 这正是 lost update：读写中间没上锁，后写悄悄吞掉了先写的结果。
这是存储层的物理故障，跟并发读写完全无关。
这是缓存调优话题，缓存 miss 不会让谁的更新被覆盖。
请求根本没发出就没有并发写，自然不存在覆盖问题。
optionExplanations_en: That is exactly lost update: no lock between read and write, so the later write quietly swallows the earlier one.
That's a physical storage failure, unrelated to concurrent reads and writes.
That's a cache-tuning topic; a cache miss never causes one update to overwrite another.
If the request was never sent there is no concurrent write, so nothing gets overwritten.
scenario_en: Two requests in the ticketing service both read available_seats = 1, decrement in application code, then write the value back.

q: 按正确顺序排列“最后一张票被卖两次”的竞态流程：
steps: Bob 在 Alice 写回前也读到还有 1 张票
Alice 和 Bob 都决定可以购买并继续扣款
两次更新都提交，库存可能到 -1，且两人都收到确认
why: 问题出在读库存和写库存之间有一个时间窗口，两个请求都基于同一个旧事实行动。同步机制的目标就是关闭这个窗口。
why_en: The race happens because both buyers act on the same stale seat count before either write closes the gap between it and the read.

scenario: 你只需要“有库存时才把库存减 1”，这个规则能直接写成当前行上的 WHERE 条件，不需要先查再判断。
q: 在数据库里落地这条规则最简单且并发安全的做法是什么？
options: 先 SELECT 查询库存，在应用代码里判断是否大于零，确认后再无条件执行一次 UPDATE 写回新库存值，中间留有并发窗口
用一条 conditional UPDATE，把 WHERE available_seats > 0 写进同一语句
给整个数据库加一把全局互斥锁，让所有并发到达的购买请求都排队串行执行
把所有并发到达的购买请求直接丢弃，统一提示用户稍后重新下单再试一次
options_en: SELECT the count first, check it's positive in application code, then run a separate unconditional UPDATE to write the new value back, leaving a concurrency window in between.
Use one conditional UPDATE that puts WHERE available_seats > 0 in the same statement.
Put a single global mutex lock on the entire database so every concurrent purchase request queues up and runs serially.
Just drop every purchase request that arrives concurrently and uniformly ask users to reorder a bit later.
why: 当检查条件就是写入行上的谓词时，数据库能在同一条 UPDATE 里完成检查和修改。失败者会匹配 0 行，而不是读到过期值再写坏它。
why_en: A conditional update makes the check and the write one atomic database operation, so the loser matches zero rows instead of overwriting a stale read.
tradeoff: 单条 WHERE 谓词的原子性 vs 应用代码里 read-then-write 的灵活性
whenOtherWins: 如果决策需要应用代码读多行、找连续座位或调用外部服务，单条 WHERE 谓词就不够，需要锁、OCC 或 reservation。

flowchart TD

  U[UPDATE where seats gt zero]
  C{Rows changed}
  S[Success]
  F[Sold out]
  R --> U --> C
  C -->|one| S

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

q_en: What is the simplest concurrency-safe way to enforce this rule in the database?
scenario_en: You only need to decrement inventory when seats remain, and that rule can be written directly as a WHERE predicate on the current row.
optionExplanations: 先读后写之间总有间隙，别人能在这个窗口插入一次写，把你的判断变成过期信息。
把 WHERE > 0 和减库存写进同一条语句，检查和修改在数据库里是一步完成的。
全局锁能兜底任意冲突，但会把所有并发请求压成串行，这里的规则不需要这么重。
直接拒绝并发请求确实零冲突，但会把大量本该成功的购买也一起挡在门外。
optionExplanations_en: There is always a gap between the read and the write, and someone else can slot a write into it before you commit.
Putting WHERE > 0 and the decrement in one statement makes the check and the write a single database step.
A global lock covers any conflict, but it serializes every request when this rule doesn't need that much.
Dropping concurrent requests avoids conflict, but it also turns away purchases that should have succeeded.

scenario: 你要用 SQL 原子地把库存减 1，只允许库存大于 0 时才能成功。
q: 哪一项最准确描述这段 SQL 的并发行为？
options: 它先无条件读一次库存，再无条件写一次新值，两次操作之间的间隙仍然会导致超卖
它把检查条件和 decrement 合成一次原子写，只有 available_seats > 0 时才会匹配
它会一直锁住整张 concerts 表，直到应用服务重启之后才会真正释放这把锁
只要这条语句被执行，它就一定会抛出异常来阻止提交，而不会返回 affected rows 为 0，靠异常回滚保证安全
options_en: It reads the count once unconditionally and writes the new value once unconditionally, so overselling can still happen in the gap between the two steps.
It merges the check and the decrement into one atomic write that only matches when available_seats is greater than 0.
It keeps the entire concerts table locked until the moment the application server eventually restarts.
As long as the statement executes, it is guaranteed to throw an exception to block the commit instead of ever returning zero affected rows, relying on that exception to stay safe.
codeSample:
UPDATE concerts
SET available_seats = available_seats - 1
WHERE concert_id = 'weeknd_tour'
  AND available_seats > 0;
why: 这是 SQL 里的 compare-and-set：条件仍成立才修改。并发失败时通常表现为 affected rows = 0，而不是业务自动回滚。
why_en: The SQL encodes compare-and-set by updating only when the current row still satisfies the predicate, so a losing write matches zero rows instead of raising an error.
tradeoff: 单条原子 UPDATE 的简单性 vs 先 SELECT 再判断的可读性
whenOtherWins: 如果还要创建 ticket 记录，必须把后续 INSERT 绑定到这条 UPDATE 是否真的改动了行，通常放在同一事务里。

q_en: Which option best describes the concurrency behavior of this SQL?
scenario_en: You want SQL to atomically decrement inventory by one, and it may only succeed when the current count is above zero.
optionExplanations: 这段代码其实是一条语句完成检查和写入，不是分成两步各自跑，所以不会留出这个超卖窗口。
这就是这条 SQL 的行为：检查和 decrement 绑在一起，只有条件仍成立才真的改动。
UPDATE 语句提交后锁就随事务释放，不会一直锁到服务重启。
条件不满足时它只是匹配 0 行、正常返回，不会抛异常。
optionExplanations_en: This SQL does the check and the write in one statement, not two separate steps, so that gap doesn't exist here.
That's exactly what it does: the check and the decrement are bundled together and only apply when the condition still holds.
The lock releases with the transaction commit, not on a server restart.
When the condition fails it just matches zero rows and returns normally instead of raising an error.

scenario: 秒杀下单用 `UPDATE ... WHERE stock > 0` 扣库存，扣减成功后才该插入 ticket 行。
q: Conditional UPDATE 匹配 0 行时，应用层最容易犯什么错误？
options: 以为 0 行会自动抛异常，于是继续无条件执行后续的 INSERT 创建 ticket
正确检查 affected row count，发现 0 行就主动回滚整个事务，不继续插入
立刻把失败原因和剩余库存一起返回给前端用户
停止对该 concert 的所有后续写入，人工介入排查
options_en: Assuming zero rows automatically raises an exception, then unconditionally running the follow-up INSERT to create the ticket.
Correctly checking the affected row count, rolling back the whole transaction when it is zero, and not proceeding to insert.
Immediately returning the failure reason and remaining inventory to the frontend.
Stopping all further writes to that concert and escalating for manual investigation.
why: UPDATE 0 rows 通常是成功执行但没有改任何行，不会自动失败。后续逻辑必须依赖 affected rows，否则会出现“没抢到座位但创建了票”。
why_en: A zero-row update usually succeeds without raising an error, so the application must check the affected count before continuing.

q_en: What mistake is application code most likely to make when a conditional UPDATE matches zero rows?
optionExplanations: 这正是常见 bug：把 0 行影响误当成会报错，于是继续无条件插入 ticket，出现有票没库存。
这是正确姿势，先看这次更新到底改了几行，再决定要不要回滚，不是那个常见错误。
把失败原因和库存回传给用户是产品体验层面的加分项，不是这里问的那种 bug。
整条业务线停写属于运维层面的过度反应，不是应用代码本身常犯的错。
optionExplanations_en: That's the classic bug: assuming zero affected rows would throw, then still running the insert unconditionally, so a ticket gets created without inventory.
That's the correct handling—check how many rows the update actually changed first, then roll back if needed—not the mistake being asked about.
Returning the failure and remaining inventory to the user is a UX nicety, not the bug this question is about.
Halting all writes on that concert is an operational overreaction, not the everyday coding mistake here.
scenario_en: A flash-sale checkout decrements stock with UPDATE ... WHERE stock > 0, and should only insert the ticket row if that update succeeded.

scenario: 你要在扣减库存成功时才创建 ticket，避免出现库存没扣成功但票被插入的情况。
q: 这段 SQL 用哪个机制来保护“扣库存”和“出票”必须同步成功？
options: INSERT 从 UPDATE 的 RETURNING 结果读取，只有那一行真的被改动才会插入
INSERT 永远无条件执行，完全不管前面的 UPDATE 究竟改动了多少行数据
COMMIT 语句会自动判断库存是否足够，并帮你补上这段业务检查逻辑
外层的这个 CTE 会让所有座位在整个 concert 的生命周期里都被永久锁定住，直到活动结束
options_en: The INSERT reads from the UPDATE's RETURNING result, so it only inserts when that row was actually changed.
The INSERT always runs unconditionally, completely regardless of how many rows the preceding UPDATE actually changed.
The COMMIT statement automatically checks whether inventory was sufficient and fills in that business-logic check for you.
This outer CTE permanently locks every seat for the concert's entire lifetime, until the event ends.
why: UPDATE 成功才 RETURNING 一行，INSERT 才有输入。这样“扣库存”和“出票”被绑定成一个事务单元，而不是两个独立的写。
why_en: The insert is driven by the update's returned row, so no ticket is created unless the guarded update actually succeeded.
tradeoff: 用 CTE+RETURNING 在 SQL 里绑定两次写 vs 在应用层查 affected rows 再决定要不要 INSERT
whenOtherWins: 如果业务逻辑在应用层更清楚，也可以检查 affected row count，失败时显式 rollback。

q_en: Which SQL mechanism makes inventory decrement and ticket creation succeed together?
scenario_en: You should create a ticket only if the inventory decrement succeeded, so a failed decrement cannot still insert a ticket.
optionExplanations: INSERT 的输入就是 UPDATE 那行 RETURNING 出来的结果，UPDATE 没改到行，INSERT 就没有输入可插。
如果 INSERT 不看 UPDATE 结果就无条件执行，扣库存失败时也会插出一张假票。
COMMIT 只负责提交已经执行完的操作，它不会替你补上库存判断逻辑。
CTE 只是这条语句里的一个临时结果集，事务提交后座位状态该怎样还是怎样，不会被永久锁住。
optionExplanations_en: The insert's input is exactly the row RETURNING hands back from the update, so no row change means no input to insert.
If the insert ran unconditionally regardless of the update's result, a failed decrement would still create a fake ticket.
COMMIT only finalizes what already ran; it doesn't add inventory-checking logic for you.
A CTE is just a temporary result set for this one statement—it doesn't leave the seat permanently locked after commit.

scenario: 售票系统允许用户挑具体座位，但库里唯一被条件更新保护的是 concerts.available_seats。
q: 只保护 concert 的 available_seats 这一个 counter，为什么仍可能把同一个座位 A15 卖出两次？
options: counter 只能回答“还有没有票”，不能回答“这个具体座位是否可用”
counter 这种整数类型永远无法在数据库里被减到 0
conditional UPDATE 语句在语法上根本不允许出现在事务里
seat_number 这一列只能存数字，不能存 'A15' 这样的字符串

An integer counter column can technically never be decremented down to zero in the database.
A conditional UPDATE statement is syntactically not allowed to appear inside a transaction.
The seat_number column can only store numbers and cannot hold a string like 'A15'.
why: Guard 必须保护真正被争抢的资源。若用户争的是 A15，就要让 A15 成为可被条件更新的 row/key，而不是只维护总数。

q_en: Why can protecting only the concert available_seats counter still sell seat A15 twice?
optionExplanations: counter 只知道还剩几张票，不知道具体是哪个座位空着，A15 这行本身根本没被这条 guard 碰到。
整数列完全可以减到 0，这不是数据库的限制。
conditional UPDATE 在事务里完全合法，这是常见写法，不存在语法限制。
seat_number 用字符串列存 'A15' 毫无问题，这是字段类型的误解。
optionExplanations_en: A counter only knows how many tickets remain, not which seat is free—A15's own row is never touched by that guard.
An integer column can absolutely be decremented to zero; that's not a real database limitation.
A conditional UPDATE is completely legal inside a transaction; there's no such syntax restriction.
Storing 'A15' in a seat_number string column works fine; that's a misunderstanding of the column type.
scenario_en: The ticketing system lets users pick a specific seat, but the only column guarded by a conditional update is concerts.available_seats.

scenario: 两个用户都想买同一个具体座位 A15，而不是随便一张任意座位的票。
q: 为了让数据库能真正拦住重复出票，条件应该写在哪个资源上？
options: seats/tickets 表里 A15 那一行，用它的 status 字段做条件写守卫
只写在 concert 的总库存 counter 上，用一个数字代表所有座位，完全不区分具体座位号
只写在用户表上，检查这个用户此前是不是已经买过一张别的票
只写在付款表上，检查这一次的付款金额是否和票价完全一致对得上
options_en: The A15 row itself in the seats/tickets table, guarding the write with its status field.
Only on the concert's total-inventory counter, using one number for every seat without distinguishing seat numbers at all.
Only on the users table, checking whether this user has already bought some other ticket before.
Only on the payments table, checking whether this payment amount exactly matches the ticket price.
why: A15 是真正被争抢的单元，所以要对它的 status 做 conditional write。总库存可以是从座位行派生出来的数据或缓存。
why_en: When the specific seat is contested, the conditional write must target that seat's own row.

scenario_en: Two users both want the exact seat A15, not just any available ticket in the venue.
optionExplanations: 两个人抢的是同一个座位号，guard 就该下在 A15 这一行的 status 上，条件写才能真的拦住第二次出票。
总库存 counter 适合卖的是任意一张票、不分座位号的场景；这里两人指定同一个座位，counter 看不出冲突。
查用户是否买过别的票只能防止同一用户重复购买，挡不住两个不同用户抢同一座位。
核对付款金额是防止多收/少收钱，跟这两个用户抢的是不是同一个座位无关。
optionExplanations_en: Both buyers want the same seat number, so the guard belongs on A15's own status—only a conditional write on that row actually blocks the second sale.
A total counter fits selling any interchangeable ticket; here two users target the same seat number, and the counter can't see that collision.
Checking a user's purchase history only stops that one user from double-buying, not two different users racing for the same seat.
Validating the payment amount guards against over/undercharging, not whether two users are racing for the same seat.

scenario: 订票平台横跨 Postgres、DynamoDB、Redis 和对外 HTTP API，想用同一套并发原语守住每处写入。
q: 下面这些不同存储上的机制，哪些本质上都在做 compare-and-set？（多选）
options: SQL 里写在 UPDATE 上的 WHERE predicate
DynamoDB 的 ConditionExpression
Redis 的 SET 命令加 NX 选项
HTTP 请求头里的 If-Match
options_en: A WHERE predicate attached to a SQL UPDATE statement.
DynamoDB's ConditionExpression on a write.
Redis's SET command with the NX option.
The If-Match header on an HTTP request.
why: 它们都表达“只有当前状态仍符合预期时才写”。具体存储不同，核心动作都是把检查和写入绑定成一步。
why_en: These mechanisms all write only if the current state still matches the expected condition, whatever store they live in.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 语句里限定哪些行会被影响的条件子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WHERE predicate is the condition clause that decides which rows a SQL statement affects.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 给写操作附加的条件表达式，只有条件满足时写入才会成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ConditionExpression is DynamoDB's way of making a write succeed only if a condition on the current item still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis SET 命令的选项，只有 key 不存在时才会写入成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NX is a Redis SET option that only writes the key if it does not already exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: ETag 是资源当前版本的标识，If-Match 请求头让服务器只在 ETag 仍匹配时才处理写请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag identifies a resource's current version, and the If-Match header makes the server apply the write only if that ETag still matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有当前值仍等于预期值时才写入的原子操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set writes a new value only if the current value still matches what you expected.

q_en: Which mechanisms across different stores are all doing compare-and-set?
optionExplanations: SQL 的 WHERE 谓词把检查条件写进同一条 UPDATE，只有那行还符合条件才会被改动。
DynamoDB 的 ConditionExpression 在写 item 前核对属性期望值，不满足就整个写入失败。
Redis SET 加 NX 只在 key 还不存在时才成功创建，天然就是一次 compare-and-set。
HTTP 的 If-Match 带上资源当前 ETag，服务端发现版本不匹配就拒绝这次写请求。
optionExplanations_en: SQL's WHERE predicate folds the check into the same UPDATE, so only a row that still matches actually gets changed.
DynamoDB's ConditionExpression checks the expected attribute value before writing the item, failing the whole write if it doesn't hold.
Redis SET with NX only succeeds in creating the key if it doesn't already exist—a compare-and-set by construction.
HTTP's If-Match sends the resource's current ETag, and the server rejects the write if the version no longer matches.
scenario_en: A booking platform spans Postgres, DynamoDB, Redis, and a public HTTP API, and you want one concurrency primitive guarding every write.
codeSample:
-- SQL: write only if the row is still free
UPDATE seats SET status='sold' WHERE id='A15' AND status='free';
-- Redis: NX = set only when the key does not exist yet
SET lock:A15 owner123 NX EX 600
-- DynamoDB: the same check expressed as a ConditionExpression
--   condition-expression "#status = :free"
-- HTTP: If-Match rejects the write once the ETag has moved
--   If-Match: "v7"

scenario: 用户要买 4 个相邻座位，应用必须先读 seat map、在代码里找出连续空位，再写入 claim；这个判断没法写成单行 WHERE 谓词。
q: 这种 read-decide-write 场景更适合用哪种并发控制方式？
options: 用 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 先锁住候选座位，再在锁内完成决策
对所有座位都无条件执行 UPDATE，完全不做任何前置判断或检查动作
只维护一个总库存 counter，完全不关心具体某个座位当前的可用状态，也不记录座位号
完全不做任何同步机制，出问题就交给客户端自己不断重试来兜底
options_en: Use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock the candidate seats first, then decide within the lock.
Run an unconditional UPDATE on every seat with no upfront check or validation at all.
Only maintain a single total-inventory counter, ignore any individual seat's current availability, and never record seat numbers.
Add no synchronization mechanism at all and leave it entirely to the client to keep retrying on its own.
why: 这是典型 read-decide-write：决策逻辑在应用代码里，数据库没法在单条 WHERE 中重新做这个判断。先锁住读到的座位，再在锁内决策。
why_en: Pessimistic locking fits read-decide-write logic that cannot be collapsed into one write predicate.
tradeoff: 锁住候选行换取安全的应用层决策 vs 单条 WHERE 谓词的零锁开销
whenOtherWins: 如果规则能写成单行谓词，conditional write 更便宜；如果冲突很少，OCC 可能更快。
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Worker A
  participant DB as DB Row
  participant B as Worker B
  A->>DB: select for update
  B->>DB: waits
  A->>DB: commit
  B->>DB: lock granted

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前假设一定会冲突，先拿锁再决策，阻止其他事务同时修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts will happen and takes a lock upfront before deciding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务内对 SELECT 出的行加行级锁，直到提交前其他事务无法修改这些行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE takes a row-level lock inside a transaction so no other transaction can change those rows until you commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 语句里限定哪些行会被影响的条件子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WHERE predicate is the condition clause that decides which rows a SQL statement affects.

q_en: Which concurrency control fits this read-decide-write case best?
scenario_en: A user wants four adjacent seats, so the app must read the seat map, find a continuous block in code, then write the claim; that logic cannot be expressed as one row predicate.
optionExplanations: 找连续座位这步判断只能在应用代码里做，所以要先用 FOR UPDATE 锁住候选行，锁着的时候座位不会被别人改变。
不做任何检查直接改，两个请求各自找到的“连续座位”可能是同一批，会真实冲突。
只看总库存完全分不出哪几个座位是连续的，这道题恰恰需要知道具体座位号。
完全不同步意味着两组人可能都以为拿到了同一片连续座位，最后谁也保不住。
optionExplanations_en: Finding a contiguous block only works in application code, so lock the candidate rows with FOR UPDATE first—while held, no one else can change them.
With no upfront check, two requests can independently pick the same block of seats and genuinely collide.
A total counter can't tell which seats are adjacent at all, and this problem specifically needs seat-level identity.
With no coordination at all, two groups can both believe they hold the same contiguous block, and neither claim is safe.

scenario: 拍卖出价要先读当前最高价、算出新价再写回，整个过程必须在一个 Postgres 事务里完成。
q: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` 在事务里的作用是什么？
options: 锁住 SELECT 选中的行，使其他事务在你提交前无法修改这些行
把这次查询自动转换成只读缓存，用来加速后续的相同查询，减少数据库压力
在数据库内部自动发起一次外部支付请求接口
把没有被选中的那些座位行从表里永久删除掉
options_en: It locks the rows the SELECT returned, so other transactions cannot modify them before you commit.
It automatically converts this query into a read-only cache that speeds up later identical queries and reduces database load.
It triggers an outbound payment API call from inside the database engine.
It permanently deletes every seat row that the SELECT did not return.
codeSample:
BEGIN;
SELECT seat_number FROM seats
WHERE concert_id = 'weeknd_tour'
  AND section = 'floor'
  AND status = 'available'
FOR UPDATE;
-- rows returned here stay locked until COMMIT/ROLLBACK
why: FOR UPDATE 是事务内的行级锁。它让你在读和写之间保持被读资源不变，但会让其他冲突事务排队等待。
why_en: SELECT FOR UPDATE locks the selected rows so other transactions cannot modify them until commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务内对 SELECT 出的行加行级锁，直到提交前其他事务无法修改这些行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE takes a row-level lock inside a transaction so no other transaction can change those rows until you commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

termDefinitions.meaning: BEGIN 到 COMMIT 之间的一组操作，要么全部生效要么全部回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of operations between BEGIN and COMMIT that either all succeed or all roll back.

q_en: What does SELECT FOR UPDATE do inside a transaction?
optionExplanations: 这就是它的作用：把 SELECT 出来的行加上行级锁，提交前谁也改不了。
FOR UPDATE 跟缓存毫无关系，它不会让查询变快或被复用。
数据库语句本身不会替你去调用外部支付接口，这不是它的职责。
它只是锁住选中的行，完全不会删除任何数据。
optionExplanations_en: That's exactly what it does: it row-locks whatever the SELECT returned, and no one else can change them before commit.
FOR UPDATE has nothing to do with caching—it doesn't speed up or reuse the query.
The database statement itself never calls an external payment API; that isn't its job.
It only locks the selected rows; it never deletes any data.
scenario_en: An auction bid has to read the current high bid, compute the new one, and write it back, all inside a single Postgres transaction.

scenario: 支付服务在事务里拿了行锁后还要调用外部支付网关，峰值每秒上千笔。
q: Pessimistic locking 常见的失败模式有哪些？（多选）
options: 锁的行太多或直接锁整张表，导致写入被串行化
持锁太久，尤其是在事务里调用慢 I/O 或外部支付 API
不同事务按不同顺序去拿多把锁，形成 deadlock
锁会让所有冲突自动消失，且不产生任何额外成本
options_en: Locking too many rows, or an entire table, which serializes writers behind one another.
Holding a lock too long, especially by calling slow I/O or an external payment API inside the transaction.
Different transactions acquiring the same set of locks in different orders, forming a deadlock.
Locks make every conflict disappear automatically and add no extra cost at all.
why: 锁的成本来自等待。锁的范围越大、持有时间越长、获取顺序越不一致，越容易造成瓶颈或 deadlock。
why_en: Pessimistic locks bottleneck throughput when they are too broad, held too long, or acquired inconsistently across transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前假设一定会冲突，先拿锁再决策，阻止其他事务同时修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts will happen and takes a lock upfront before deciding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个事务互相持有对方需要的锁，永久等待对方释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when transactions hold locks that the others are waiting for, so none of them can proceed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

q_en: What are common failure modes of pessimistic locking?
optionExplanations: 锁的范围越大，越多本来无关的写入也要排队等它释放。
锁里塞慢 I/O 或外部调用，等待的人跟着被这次调用的延迟拖住。
两个事务反着顺序拿两把锁，各自等对方手里的那把，谁也走不了。
锁本身要付出等待和吞吐代价，不可能让冲突免费消失。
optionExplanations_en: The wider the lock's scope, the more unrelated writes end up queued behind it.
Slow I/O or an external call inside a lock drags every waiter down by that call's latency.
Two transactions grab the same two locks in opposite order, each waiting on what the other holds, and neither can proceed.
Locking always costs waiting and throughput; conflicts don't vanish for free.
scenario_en: A payment service holds a row lock inside its transaction while it calls an external payment gateway, at a peak of thousands per second.

scenario: 你在座位锁事务中要调用外部 payment API，支付调用可能耗时几秒甚至更久。
q: 在持有数据库锁期间处理这次支付调用，更好的设计原则是什么？
options: 绝不在持有数据库锁时做慢 I/O；支付调用放在拿锁前或释放锁之后
把这把锁一直持有 10 分钟，直到用户离开支付页面为止
为了简单，直接把整张 seats 表都锁住再调用支付接口，等支付返回再放开
让所有排队等待同一座位的买家都同步等待同一次支付调用返回
options_en: Never do slow I/O while holding a database lock; call the payment API before acquiring it or after releasing it.
Hold that lock continuously for 10 minutes until the user leaves the payment page.
For simplicity, lock the entire seats table before calling the payment endpoint, releasing it only after payment returns.
Make every buyer waiting on the same seat block synchronously on that one payment call's response.
why: 慢 I/O 会把所有等待同一资源的事务拖住。数据库锁应该覆盖最小行集和最短时间，而不是外部调用的整个耗时。
why_en: Do not hold database locks across slow I/O, because every waiter inherits that external call's latency.
tradeoff: 把慢 I/O 挪出锁的范围 vs 图省事把支付调用塞进事务里
whenOtherWins: 如果需要跨支付等待保留座位，应该用带 TTL 的 reservation/distributed lock，而不是事务锁。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立于单个数据库事务存在的租约记录，谁持有、何时过期，任何服务器都能读到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a lease record that lives outside any single database transaction, so any server can see who holds it and when it expires.

q_en: What is the better design principle while a database lock would cover a payment call?
scenario_en: Your seat-locking transaction would call an external payment API, and that payment call may take several seconds or longer.
optionExplanations: 支付调用挪到拿锁前或释放锁之后，锁只覆盖真正需要原子保护的那一小步。
把锁攥着等用户填完支付，队列里所有人都得跟着这十分钟一起等。
为了一次支付调用锁住整张表，代价远超这条规则本身需要的保护范围。
让所有排队的买家一起卡在同一次支付调用上，等于把一个人的慢请求变成全场的慢请求。
optionExplanations_en: Move the payment call before acquiring the lock or after releasing it, so the lock only covers the small step that truly needs atomic protection.
Holding the lock while the user fills out payment makes every other waiter inherit that ten minutes.
Locking the whole table just to make one payment call costs far more than this rule actually needs.
Making every queued buyer block on one payment call turns one person's slow request into everyone's slow request.

scenario: 转账服务在一个事务里按参数到达顺序，依次锁住转出账户行和转入账户行。
q: 银行转账里 Alice->Bob 和 Bob->Alice 同时发生，为什么可能 deadlock？
options: 两个事务按相反顺序去拿两个账户的锁，各自持有一把并等待另一把
数据库这种系统本身根本不支持存储账户余额这类数值，只能存文本字段
转账这种操作在设计上一定完全不需要用到事务
只是因为两笔转账里出现的用户名字碰巧不一样而已
options_en: The two transactions acquire the two account locks in opposite orders, each holding one and waiting on the other.
Databases as a category of system cannot store numeric values like account balances at all, only text fields.
A transfer operation is designed to never need a transaction wrapping it under any circumstances.
It's simply because the two transfers happen to involve users with different names.
why: 循环等待是 deadlock 的核心。事务 A 锁 Alice 等 Bob，事务 B 锁 Bob 等 Alice，双方都无法继续。
why_en: Deadlock occurs when transactions acquire the same locks in opposite orders and end up waiting on each other.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[A locks Alice]
  B[B locks Bob]
  C[A waits for Bob]
  D[B waits for Alice]
  X[Deadlock]
  A --> C --> X
  B --> D --> X

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个事务互相持有对方需要的锁，永久等待对方释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when transactions hold locks that the others are waiting for, so none of them can proceed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

termDefinitions.meaning: BEGIN 到 COMMIT 之间的一组操作，要么全部生效要么全部回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a group of operations between BEGIN and COMMIT that either all succeed or all roll back.

q_en: Why can simultaneous Alice-to-Bob and Bob-to-Alice bank transfers deadlock?
optionExplanations: 两笔转账各自持有对方需要的那把账户锁，方向相反就形成了谁也让不出来的循环等待。
数据库存储数值余额是最基本的能力，这不是限制。
转账天然需要事务保证两个账户的改动同生共死，说不需要事务是错的。
两笔转账的用户名字不同跟锁的获取顺序毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Each transfer holds the account lock the other one needs, and opposite directions create a circular wait where neither side can yield.
Storing numeric balances is the most basic thing a database does; that's not a real limitation.
A transfer needs a transaction precisely so both account changes succeed or fail together; saying otherwise is wrong.
The two transfers' usernames being different has nothing to do with the order locks are acquired in.
scenario_en: The transfer service locks the debit account row and then the credit account row, in whatever order the parameters happen to arrive.

scenario: 多个转账事务需要同时锁定两位用户的账户行，但发起转账的方向可能相反。
q: 预防这种 deadlock 的标准做法是什么？
options: 所有事务按全局一致的顺序拿锁，比如永远按 user_id 从小到大排序
永远先锁住这次操作的发起人，再锁对方
每次转账都随机决定先锁哪一个账户
完全不处理数据库抛出的 deadlock 错误，让它直接失败，把报错抛给用户
options_en: Every transaction acquires locks in one globally consistent order, such as always sorting by user_id ascending.
Always lock the account that initiated this particular transfer first, then the other one.
Randomly decide which account to lock first on every transfer.
Never handle the deadlock error the database raises, just let the transaction fail, and surface the raw error to the user.
codeSample:
-- always lock the lower id first, regardless of who initiated the transfer
SELECT * FROM accounts
WHERE id IN (123, 456)
ORDER BY id
FOR UPDATE;
why: 所有事务按同一确定性顺序获取资源，循环等待就形成不了。即便如此，仍要把数据库的 deadlock abort 当作可重试错误处理。
why_en: Consistent lock ordering prevents circular waits, and deadlock errors should still be caught and retried.
tradeoff: 全局一致的锁顺序 vs 按业务发起方向天然的加锁顺序
whenOtherWins: 如果每次事务只锁单行资源，deadlock 风险本来就很小；跨多个资源才必须明确锁顺序。

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有事务按同一个全局固定顺序获取锁，避免循环等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ordered locking means every transaction acquires locks in the same global order so a circular wait cannot form.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个事务互相持有对方需要的锁，永久等待对方释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock is when transactions hold locks that the others are waiting for, so none of them can proceed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

q_en: What is the standard way to prevent this deadlock?
scenario_en: Several transfer transactions need to lock two account rows, but the transfer direction can be opposite.
optionExplanations: 所有事务都按同一个固定顺序（比如 user_id 从小到大）拿锁，循环等待在结构上就不可能出现。
发起人不同、方向可能相反，按发起人排序等于顺序还是会反过来。
顺序是随机的，两个事务照样可能凑成互相等待的组合，风险没有降低。
不处理 deadlock 错误只是让失败变成用户能看到的原始报错，不是预防手段。
optionExplanations_en: Every transaction acquires locks in the same fixed order (say, ascending user_id), so a circular wait can't structurally form.
The initiator differs by transaction, so ordering by initiator can still end up reversed between two transfers.
With a random order, two transactions can still land on opposite sequences and deadlock just as easily.
Not handling the deadlock error just surfaces a raw failure to the user; it isn't a prevention technique.

scenario: 协作文档的元数据一天只被改几次，冲突极少，但任何一次修改都不能被悄悄覆盖。
q: Optimistic concurrency control 的基本假设是什么？
options: 冲突比较少见，所以先放大家去执行，写入时用 version 检测冲突再决定重试
冲突总是非常频繁，所以要先无差别地阻塞住全部到达的并发写请求和流量，全部串行执行
数据库表结构设计上完全不需要额外设计任何用于比较的版本字段
所有写入操作都可以互相无条件地直接覆盖，完全不用管先后的顺序
options_en: Conflicts are rare, so let everyone proceed and detect conflicts at write time with a version check, retrying if needed.
Conflicts are always extremely frequent, so every incoming concurrent write request must be blocked indiscriminately upfront and serialized.
The table schema design never needs any additional version field at all for comparison purposes.
Every write operation is allowed to unconditionally overwrite every other write, with no regard for ordering at all.
why: OCC 不提前拿锁，而是在写入时检查“我读到的版本是否仍然是当前版本”。低冲突场景下能避免锁等待。
why_en: Optimistic concurrency assumes conflicts are rare and detects them with a version check at write time instead of locking upfront.

q_en: What is the basic assumption behind optimistic concurrency control?
optionExplanations: OCC 就是赌冲突很少见：先让大家都跑，写入那一刻用 version 核对，撞车了再重试。
先无差别阻塞所有请求描述的是悲观锁的假设，不是 OCC。
没有可比较的版本字段，OCC 根本没法检测出冲突。
无条件互相覆盖会直接产生 lost update，这正是 OCC 想避免的结果。
optionExplanations_en: OCC bets that conflicts are rare: let everyone proceed, check the version at write time, and retry only on a real collision.
Blocking every request upfront describes pessimistic locking's assumption, not OCC's.
Without a comparable version field, OCC has nothing to detect a conflict with.
Unconditional overwrites produce exactly the lost updates OCC is trying to prevent.

scenario: 多个管理员偶尔编辑同一个产品描述，冲突很少发生，读写比例很高。
q: 在这种低冲突、读多写少的场景下，哪种并发控制通常最合适？
options: OCC：用 version 或 ETag 检测冲突，冲突时再重试
对这张表加一把长时间持有的分布式锁
把所有相关事务都强制设成 SERIALIZABLE 隔离级别
用一个全局队列把所有编辑请求串行化处理
options_en: OCC: detect conflicts with a version or ETag, and retry only when one actually happens.
Put a long-held distributed lock on that table.
Force every related transaction into SERIALIZABLE isolation.
Route every edit request through a single global queue to serialize them.
why: 低冲突场景不值得为每次写都先付锁的成本。OCC 让无冲突路径很快，偶尔冲突再重试或提示用户。
why_en: OCC fits rare-conflict edits because the common path avoids blocking and only retries on the occasional conflict.
tradeoff: 低冲突下零阻塞的乐观重试 vs 每次写都先排队的悲观锁
whenOtherWins: 如果同一资源持续高并发争抢，重试会堆积，悲观锁或队列串行化更可控。

q_en: Which concurrency control usually fits this low-conflict, read-heavy case?
scenario_en: Several admins occasionally edit the same product description, conflicts are rare, and the workload is mostly reads.
optionExplanations: 冲突本来就少，让常见路径零阻塞地跑完，只在偶尔撞车时靠 version/ETag 检测后重试，成本最低。

optionExplanations_en: Conflicts are rare here, so let the common path run unblocked and only detect the occasional collision with a version/ETag check and retry—cheapest option.
A distributed lock fits long flows that span waits or external calls; editing a product description in milliseconds doesn't need that machinery.
SERIALIZABLE exists for cross-row invariants; an occasional same-row edit conflict doesn't need isolation that strong.
A global queue caps every edit at one worker's speed, which wastes throughput when concurrent edits are rare anyway.

scenario: Alice 读到 version=42 后尝试更新；如果别人先改过这一行，version 就已经不是 42 了。
q: 这段 SQL 是怎么检测出并发冲突的？
options: WHERE version = 42 让基于旧版本的写只会匹配 0 行，应用检查后再回滚或重试
它会直接忽略掉 version 这一列，强制用新值覆盖掉旧的值
它只检查 available_seats 是否大于零，完全不会去检查 version，撞车也照样写入
只要提交一失败，它就会自动阻塞并等待 10 分钟之后重发
options_en: WHERE version = 42 makes a write based on a stale version match zero rows, and the app checks that before rolling back or retrying.
It ignores the version column entirely and forcibly overwrites the old value with the new one.
It only checks whether available_seats is greater than zero and never looks at version at all, writing even on a conflict.
The moment a commit fails, it automatically blocks and resends the exact same write ten minutes later.
codeSample:
UPDATE concerts
SET available_seats = available_seats - 1,
    version = version + 1
WHERE concert_id = 'weeknd_tour'
  AND version = 42;
why: 版本列每次写都会递增。写入时版本不匹配说明这一行已经被别人改过，这次操作必须失败、重读或重试。
why_en: The version predicate detects stale writes because any intervening update changes the version.
tradeoff: 加一列 version 换取可靠的冲突检测 vs 不加列、直接靠业务字段自己做比较
whenOtherWins: 如果规则能用单条 conditional write 表达，不一定需要额外 version 列；如果冲突很高，锁可能更便宜。

scenario: 你要给订单行加 OCC 版本检查，候选是 version 列、updated_at，或直接复用某个业务字段。
q: 哪些值可以安全地当作 OCC 的版本检查依据？（多选）

每次写都会真的变化、且分辨率足够精细的 updated_at 时间戳

options_en: A dedicated, always-incrementing version column.
An updated_at timestamp that genuinely changes on every write and has fine enough resolution.
A monotonically increasing business value that never moves backward, like the current high bid in an auction.
An ordinary business value that can go A to B and back to A, with no extra protection.
why: 版本值必须能可靠反映中间写入。专用递增列最安全；普通业务值可能出现 ABA，不能随便复用。
why_en: A version token must change reliably on every write, and a dedicated incrementing column is the safest default choice.

只要分辨率够细、且每次写真的会变，updated_at 也能当版本用；分辨率太粗就会漏掉中间写。
拍卖最高价只会单调上升，本身就能当版本比较，不用额外加列。
普通业务值可能从 A 变到 B 又变回 A，只做相等比较会误以为中间什么都没发生。

An auction's high bid only moves upward, so it can double as the version without adding a column.
An ordinary business value can go from A to B and back to A, and an equality check alone would miss that round trip.

q_en: What exactly is the ABA problem in OCC?
optionExplanations: 值从 A 变到 B 又变回 A，只做相等比较的检查看不出中间发生过写入，这就是 ABA。
两把锁按相同顺序获取是避免 deadlock 的做法，跟版本检查无关。
队列只配一个 worker 是串行化模式，不是版本比较问题。
key 因为设了存活时长而自动清理，这是租约到期，不是值的往返变化。
optionExplanations_en: A value moves from A to B and back to A, and an equality check alone can't see that a write happened in between—that's ABA.
Acquiring two locks in the same order is a deadlock-prevention technique, unrelated to version checks.
A queue with one worker is a serialization pattern, not a version-comparison issue.
A key getting cleaned up once its lifetime runs out is a lease lapsing, not a value making a round trip.
scenario_en: An auction uses the current high bid as its OCC version, and bids can be retracted so that value can fall back down.

scenario: 热门演唱会一开票，同一行库存每秒被上万请求争抢，几乎每次尝试都会撞车。
q: 在高冲突场景下，为什么 pessimistic locking 往往比 OCC 更合适？
options: OCC 在高冲突下会产生大量失败重试，浪费的工作量可能超过提前排队等待锁的成本
因为 OCC 这种机制在原理上永远都无法保证数据最终的正确性和一致性，必然丢更新
因为使用行锁完全不会降低系统整体的并发处理能力和吞吐量
因为 OCC 这种机制在设计上只能被用来处理只读的查询请求场景
options_en: Under high contention, OCC produces heavy failed-retry churn, and the wasted work can exceed the cost of just queuing on a lock upfront.
Because OCC as a mechanism can never, by its very design, guarantee eventual data correctness, so it inevitably loses updates.
Because taking a row lock never reduces the system's overall concurrency or throughput at all.
Because OCC as a mechanism is, by design, only ever applicable to read-only query scenarios.
why: OCC 的优势是低冲突时不阻塞；高冲突时大家都写失败再重试，浪费工作量。锁 upfront 排队反而更可预测。
why_en: Under high contention, optimistic retries can waste more work than simply locking up front and letting requests queue.
tradeoff: OCC 的零阻塞乐观重试 vs pessimistic locking 的排队可预测性
whenOtherWins: 如果同一资源的写冲突很少发生，OCC 完全不用排队，性能明显更好。

q_en: Why is pessimistic locking often a better fit than OCC under high contention?
optionExplanations: 高冲突下大家都写完才发现失败又要重试，反复浪费的工作量可能比一开始排队等锁还大。
OCC 只要写时能正确检测冲突，最终结果照样是正确的，这个说法是反的。
拿行锁必然让别的事务排队等待，说它不影响并发是错的。
OCC 一样能保护写路径，不是只能用在只读查询上。
optionExplanations_en: Under heavy contention, everyone finishes the work only to fail and retry, and that repeated waste can exceed the cost of just queuing on a lock.
As long as OCC correctly detects conflicts at write time, the final result is still correct—this claim has it backwards.
Taking a row lock necessarily makes other transactions wait; claiming it doesn't affect concurrency is wrong.
OCC protects write paths just as well; it isn't limited to read-only queries.
scenario_en: When a hot concert goes on sale, tens of thousands of requests a second hit the same inventory row, so almost every attempt collides.

scenario: 排班系统要求任意时刻至少 1 名医生 on call；两名医生同时请假，各自都查到对方还在岗。
q: Write skew 具体指的是哪种冲突？
options: 两个事务读取的是重叠集合，写的却是不同行，各自看都合法，合起来却破坏了跨行约束
两个事务同时写同一行数据，触发了数据库普通的 version 检查冲突，立刻被拦下
某个 Redis key 因为设置的过期时间到了而被自动删除掉
数据库所在服务器磁盘剩余空间严重不足，导致这次写入被拒绝
options_en: Two transactions read an overlapping set of rows but write different rows, each valid alone yet jointly violating a cross-row invariant.
Two transactions write the same row at the same time, trigger an ordinary database version-check conflict, and are caught immediately.
A Redis key gets automatically deleted because its set lifetime ran out.
The database server's disk runs critically low on free space, so this write gets rejected.
why: Write skew 的难点是没有同一行冲突。条件写、行锁、version check 都可能看不到“读集合被别人改变”这件事。
why_en: Write skew happens when transactions write different rows but jointly violate an invariant based on overlapping reads.

q_en: What kind of conflict is write skew?
optionExplanations: 两个事务各自读到的数据有重叠，但写的是不同行，单独看都合法，合起来却破坏了跨行的约束，这就是 write skew。
写同一行触发的是普通的 version 冲突，行锁或条件写就能抓住，不叫 write skew。
key 因为存活时长到了被清理是缓存租约的事，跟事务隔离无关。
磁盘空间不足是容量层面的故障，不是并发逻辑问题。
optionExplanations_en: Both transactions read overlapping data but write different rows—each valid alone, yet together they break a cross-row rule. That's write skew.
Two writes to the same row trigger an ordinary version conflict that a row lock or conditional write already catches; that isn't write skew.
A key getting cleaned up once its lifetime runs out is a cache-lease matter, unrelated to transaction isolation.
Low disk space is a capacity failure, not a concurrency-logic issue.
scenario_en: An on-call system must always keep at least one doctor on duty, and two doctors request leave at the same moment, each seeing the other still on.

scenario: On-call 表要求团队至少有一人值班；Alice 和 Bob 各自读到对方仍在值班，于是同时把自己改成 inactive，两次写的是不同行。
q: 哪种机制能让数据库真正捕获这种没有共享写入行的 write skew？
options: SERIALIZABLE 隔离级别，并把由它引发的 serialization error 当作可重试错误
只给 Alice 这一行数据单独加一个 version 字段来做检查
只对 Bob 这一行单独执行 conditional UPDATE 条件更新，完全不管 Alice 那一行数据的状态
把整条路径上所有相关事务的隔离级别都直接降到最弱的 READ UNCOMMITTED
options_en: SERIALIZABLE isolation, treating the serialization error it raises as a retryable failure.
Only add a version field to Alice's row by itself and check just that.
Only run a conditional UPDATE on Bob's row by itself, completely ignoring the state of Alice's row.
Downgrade every related transaction on this whole path straight to the weakest option, READ UNCOMMITTED.
why: Write skew 没有共享写入行，弱隔离级别看不到冲突。SERIALIZABLE 让结果等价于事务串行执行，因此会中止其中一个。
why_en: Serializable isolation catches write skew by ensuring the result matches some serial order of the transactions.
tradeoff: SERIALIZABLE 捕获跨行约束的能力 vs 它带来的依赖追踪和 abort/retry 成本
whenOtherWins: 如果能把“至少一人值班”物化到 team row 的计数或锁上，单行 guard/lock 往往比全事务 SERIALIZABLE 更便宜。

q_en: Which mechanism lets the database catch write skew when no row is written by both transactions?
scenario_en: An on-call table requires at least one engineer to stay active; Alice and Bob each see the other as active, then both set themselves inactive in separate rows.
optionExplanations: 这个隔离级别会让每笔事务的效果如同排队逐一执行，跨行冲突一出现就直接中止其中一方，应用接到错误后重试。
只查 Alice 这一行看不到 Bob 那边发生的改动，两人各自的读写集合没被真正比对。
只保护 Bob 一样漏掉 Alice 的改动，单行 guard 抓不住跨行的读集合冲突。
READ UNCOMMITTED 是最弱隔离，只会让脏读更容易发生，完全帮不上这道题。
optionExplanations_en: This isolation level makes every transaction's effect look like it ran in a queue one at a time, aborting one side the instant a cross-row conflict shows up so the app can retry.
Checking only Alice's row misses whatever Bob changed—their overlapping read sets are never actually compared.
Guarding only Bob's row misses Alice's change the same way; a single-row guard can't catch a cross-row read-set conflict.
READ UNCOMMITTED is the weakest isolation level and only makes dirty reads easier, which doesn't help here at all.

scenario: 面试官追问你打算怎么在关系数据库里选隔离级别来处理并发写冲突，你需要说出数据库通常提供的几个标准选项。
q: 关系数据库通常提供哪些标准隔离级别？（多选）
options: READ UNCOMMITTED
READ COMMITTED
REPEATABLE READ
SERIALIZABLE
options_en: READ UNCOMMITTED
READ COMMITTED
REPEATABLE READ
SERIALIZABLE
why: 这四个是常见关系数据库的标准隔离级别。能捕获 write skew 的通常只有 SERIALIZABLE，较弱的级别都会漏掉。
why_en: The common SQL isolation levels are read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, and serializable, with only serializable catching write skew.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最弱的隔离级别，能读到其他事务尚未提交、随时可能回滚的改动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: READ UNCOMMITTED is the weakest isolation level, letting you see another transaction's uncommitted changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只能看到其他事务已经提交的改动；PostgreSQL 的默认级别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: READ COMMITTED only lets you see changes other transactions have already committed, and it is PostgreSQL's default.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一事务内重复读同一行会得到一致结果；MySQL 的默认级别。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REPEATABLE READ guarantees repeated reads of the same row stay consistent within one transaction, and it is MySQL's default.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到了另一个事务尚未提交、随时可能回滚的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dirty read means reading data from another transaction that has not committed yet and might still roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个事务各自读到重叠的数据集合、写不同的行，单独看都合法，合起来却破坏了跨行的业务约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write skew is when two transactions read overlapping data and write different rows, each valid alone but jointly violating an invariant.

q_en: Which standard isolation levels do relational databases usually provide?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how you would choose a relational database isolation level for concurrent writes, so you need to name the standard choices.
optionExplanations: READ UNCOMMITTED 允许读到别的事务还没提交、随时可能回滚的数据，开销最低但风险最高。
READ COMMITTED 只能看见已提交的改动，是 PostgreSQL 的默认级别。
REPEATABLE READ 保证同一事务内重复读到一致结果，是 MySQL 的默认级别。
SERIALIZABLE 是最强级别，结果等价于事务逐个串行执行，能捕获 write skew。
optionExplanations_en: READ UNCOMMITTED lets you see another transaction's uncommitted, possibly-rolled-back data—cheapest but riskiest.
READ COMMITTED only shows already-committed changes and is PostgreSQL's default.
REPEATABLE READ guarantees consistent repeated reads within one transaction and is MySQL's default.
SERIALIZABLE is the strongest level, equivalent to running transactions one at a time, and it catches write skew.

scenario: 订票库并发很高，团队想直接把所有写路径设成一个隔离级别，一劳永逸地解决竞态。
q: 为什么不应该默认把所有高并发路径都设成 SERIALIZABLE？
options: 它需要数据库额外跟踪读写依赖，冲突时 abort/retry，是几种机制里成本最高的
因为 SERIALIZABLE 提供的隔离保证实际上比 READ COMMITTED 更弱
因为 SERIALIZABLE 这种隔离级别只能用在 Redis 这类内存存储上
因为它天生就没有能力处理任何跨行的业务约束
options_en: It makes the database track extra read/write dependencies and abort/retry on conflict, making it the most expensive option here.
Because SERIALIZABLE actually provides weaker guarantees than READ COMMITTED.
Because SERIALIZABLE as an isolation level only applies to in-memory stores like Redis.
Because it is inherently incapable of handling any cross-row business invariant.
why: SERIALIZABLE 能覆盖更复杂的冲突，但会增加开销和重试。能用 conditional write、锁或 OCC 解决时，通常这些更便宜。
why_en: Serializable isolation is powerful but expensive because it tracks dependencies and may abort work that has to be redone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

q_en: Why should you not default every high-concurrency path to SERIALIZABLE?
optionExplanations: 它要多跟踪读写依赖，冲突时 abort 再重试，这几种机制里它的开销最高。
SERIALIZABLE 是最强隔离级别，比 READ COMMITTED 更严格，这个说法反了。
它是关系数据库的隔离级别概念，和 Redis 这种内存存储完全不是一回事。
它恰恰是唯一能可靠捕获跨行约束的隔离级别，说它做不到是错的。
optionExplanations_en: It has to track extra read/write dependencies and abort/retry on conflict, making it the priciest option here.
SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, stricter than READ COMMITTED—this claim has it backwards.
It's a relational-database isolation-level concept, entirely different from an in-memory store like Redis.
It's actually the one isolation level that reliably catches cross-row invariants; claiming it can't is wrong.
scenario_en: The ticketing database runs hot, and the team wants to set every write path to one isolation level and be done with races.

scenario: 一个约束本来跨多行，例如 team 至少要有一个 active on-call engineer，但你想避免每次都用昂贵的 SERIALIZABLE 事务。
q: 更便宜的重构思路是什么？
options: 把跨行约束物化到单个 team row 上，比如维护一个 active_count 字段
让每个 engineer 行各自独立无保护地更新，彼此完全不做任何交叉检查
把整个系统里所有路径的隔离级别，一律降到最弱的 READ UNCOMMITTED，牺牲全部隔离
干脆把“至少一人值班”这条业务约束直接从系统里删掉，不再检查
options_en: Materialize the cross-row invariant onto a single team row, such as an active_count field.
Let each engineer row update independently with no protection and no cross-checking between them at all.
Downgrade every path in the whole system to the weakest isolation level, READ UNCOMMITTED, sacrificing all isolation.
Just delete the 'at least one on-call' business rule from the system entirely and stop checking it.
why: 数据库只能保护它能看见的冲突。把跨行约束落到一个可锁/可条件更新的 row，就回到了单资源 contention，工具都能直接用。
why_en: Materializing a cross-row invariant onto one row turns it into a conflict the database can guard directly.
tradeoff: 把约束收敛成单行 guard 的低成本 vs 用 SERIALIZABLE 兜底任意跨行约束的通用性
whenOtherWins: 如果约束天然复杂、难以物化到一行，SERIALIZABLE 或业务级补偿逻辑可能仍然必要。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把原本跨多行才能判断的约束，收敛成落在单一行/key 上就能检查的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Materializing the invariant means collapsing a cross-row rule into a single row or key the database can check directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务内对 SELECT 出的行加行级锁，直到提交前其他事务无法修改这些行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE takes a row-level lock inside a transaction so no other transaction can change those rows until you commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

q_en: What is the cheaper refactoring idea here?
scenario_en: A constraint spans multiple rows, such as requiring at least one active on-call engineer, but you want to avoid an expensive SERIALIZABLE transaction every time.
optionExplanations: 把“至少一人值班”收敛成 team 行上的 active_count，冲突就变成了单行 conditional write，用便宜的工具就能保护。
各自改自己的行、互不检查，两人还是可能同时把自己设成 inactive，约束照样被破坏。
把隔离级别降到最弱只会让更多种冲突都检测不到，跟解决这个问题的方向相反。
直接删掉“至少一人值班”这条规则是放弃正确性，不是重构。
optionExplanations_en: Collapsing 'at least one on-call' into an active_count on the team row turns the conflict into a single-row conditional write that cheap tools can guard.
Letting each engineer row update alone with no cross-check still lets both go inactive at once and breaks the invariant.
Downgrading isolation to the weakest level only makes more kinds of conflicts undetectable—the opposite direction of a fix.
Deleting the 'at least one on-call' rule abandons correctness; it isn't a refactor.

scenario: 购物车里的座位要 hold 住 10 分钟，用户在这期间跨多次请求走完选座和付款。
q: Distributed lock 和数据库事务里的行锁，关键区别是什么？
options: Distributed lock 是有独立生命周期的租约记录，可以跨等待、外部调用或多个步骤存在
Distributed lock 只能存在于单个 SQL 事务内部，事务结束它就消失，跨请求就失效了
Distributed lock 不需要设置任何过期时间，也不需要显式释放
Distributed lock 只能用来保护只读的查询请求
options_en: A distributed lock is a lease with its own independent lifetime that can span a wait, an external call, or multiple steps.
A distributed lock can only exist inside a single SQL transaction and disappears when it ends, so it cannot span requests.
A distributed lock needs no expiration time and never needs to be explicitly released.
A distributed lock can only be used to protect read-only queries.
why: 数据库锁随事务结束释放，不适合 10 分钟的 checkout 流程。Distributed lock 把“谁持有资源、何时过期”存成数据，让所有服务器可见。
why_en: A distributed lock is a lease with its own lifetime, unlike a transaction lock that ends the moment the database transaction does.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立于单个数据库事务存在的租约记录，谁持有、何时过期，任何服务器都能读到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a lease record that lives outside any single database transaction, so any server can see who holds it and when it expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带有效期的临时持有权，到期后自动失效，不需要显式释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lease is a temporary right to hold something that automatically expires without needing an explicit release.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

q_en: What is the key difference between a distributed lock and a database row lock?
optionExplanations: 它是一份独立于任何数据库事务的租约记录，可以跨越等待、外部调用甚至多个处理步骤持续保持有效。
这描述的其实是数据库行锁，行锁才随事务结束而释放。
没有过期时间又不显式释放的锁一旦持有者崩溃就永远锁死，这是危险设计不是特点。
它通常用来保护并发写入，而不是保护只读查询，这跟锁的定位刚好相反。
optionExplanations_en: It's a lease record independent of any single database transaction, staying valid across a wait, an external call, or several processing steps.
That actually describes a database row lock, which releases when its transaction ends.
A lock with no expiration and no explicit release just stays locked forever if the holder crashes—that's a dangerous design, not a feature.
It's typically there to protect concurrent writes, not to protect read-only queries—the opposite of what this claims.

scenario: Ticketmaster 用户选中座位 A15 后需要大约 10 分钟填写支付信息，这期间不能让别人抢走这个座位。
q: 应该用什么机制同时保护用户体验和数据正确性？
options: 在事务内用 FOR UPDATE 把这个座位锁住整整 10 分钟，一直到用户完成支付流程为止
带 TTL 的 reservation，记录 reserved_by 和 reserved_until
什么都不做，等用户填完全部支付信息并提交之后再去检查这个座位是否还在
只依赖 concert 的总库存 counter 这一个数字，完全不单独跟踪这个座位本身的实时状态
options_en: Hold a FOR UPDATE lock on that seat inside a database transaction for the full ten minutes until the payment process finishes.
A TTL reservation recording reserved_by and reserved_until.
Do nothing and only check whether the seat is still available after the user finishes filling out and submitting payment.
Rely only on the concert's single total-inventory counter number, without tracking this individual seat's real-time state at all.
why: 长时间用户等待不应持有数据库事务锁。带 TTL 的 reservation 让座位短期被占用，超时自动释放，也避免用户填完支付才发现座位没了。
why_en: Seat checkout needs a TTL reservation rather than a long-held database transaction lock.
tradeoff: 带 TTL 的 reservation 能跨越用户等待和外部调用 vs 事务锁只在单个事务内有效但零额外基础设施
whenOtherWins: 如果只是毫秒级的 read-decide-write，FOR UPDATE 或 conditional write 更简单，不需要分布式锁。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE takes a row-level lock inside a transaction so no other transaction can change those rows until you commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

q_en: Which mechanism protects both user experience and data correctness?
scenario_en: A Ticketmaster user selects seat A15 and needs about ten minutes to enter payment details; nobody else should grab that seat during that window.
optionExplanations: 事务锁只该覆盖毫秒级的判断，把它撑满用户填支付的十分钟，会让所有等这个座位的人跟着排队十分钟。
这条记录本身带着存活时长，写明谁占用、占到什么时候，用户超时不付款就自动清掉，不需要长期占着数据库事务锁。
什么都不检查、等提交才查座位，等于让用户填完十分钟表单才发现白填了，体验很差。
只看总库存分不出具体是哪个座位被占用，两个人还是可能同时选中 A15。
optionExplanations_en: A transaction lock should only cover a millisecond-scale check; stretching it across ten minutes of payment entry queues everyone else behind that one seat.
This record itself carries its own lifetime, naming who holds it and until when, clearing itself automatically if the user never pays, with no long-held transaction lock.
Checking nothing until submission means the user only discovers the seat is gone after filling out ten minutes of payment details—a poor experience.
A total counter can't tell which specific seat is held, so two people can still both land on A15.

scenario: 你想用 Redis 实现一个短期的座位 hold：只允许没人持有时创建，并且要能自动过期，不用后台清理 job。
q: 这条 Redis 命令形态里，最关键的两个元素分别是什么？
options: SET 命令搭配 NX 选项和 TTL/EX 选项
先 GET 一次再无条件执行 SET，不加任何选项
用 KEYS * 扫描全库找出所有已存在的座位 key
只用 DEL 命令，删除后立即让别人重新写入
options_en: The SET command combined with the NX option and a TTL/EX option.
A GET followed by an unconditional SET, with no options at all.
Scanning the whole keyspace with KEYS * to find every existing seat key.
Just the DEL command, deleting the key so someone else can immediately write it.
codeSample:
SET seat:A15:hold user123 NX EX 600
-- NX: only set if the key does not already exist
-- EX 600: expire after 600 seconds (10 minutes)
-- returns nil if someone else already holds it
why: NX 保证 key 不存在时才创建，TTL/EX 保证 holder 崩溃或放弃后自动释放。缺少 NX 会让后来的请求覆盖已有锁。
why_en: Redis SET with NX and an expiration atomically creates a lock only if it does not already exist, and clears it automatically.
tradeoff: Redis TTL lock 的速度和零运维 vs 数据库 reservation 列的一致性更强
whenOtherWins: 如果 double-grant 会破坏核心数据一致性，普通 Redis TTL lock 可能不够强，需要数据库条件写或 ZooKeeper/etcd。

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis SET 命令的选项，只有 key 不存在时才会写入成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NX is a Redis SET option that only writes the key if it does not already exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis SET 命令里设置过期秒数的选项，到期后 key 自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EX is the Redis SET option that sets an expiration in seconds so the key deletes itself automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立于单个数据库事务存在的租约记录，谁持有、何时过期，任何服务器都能读到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a lease record that lives outside any single database transaction, so any server can see who holds it and when it expires.

q_en: What are the two key elements in this Redis command shape?
scenario_en: You want Redis to implement a short-lived seat hold: create it only when nobody holds it, and let it expire automatically without a cleanup job.
optionExplanations: NX 保证只有没人占用时才建这个 key，EX 保证 holder 消失后也会自己清掉，两个选项缺一不可。
先 GET 再无条件 SET，中间的空档照样能被别人插进来抢到 key。
KEYS * 是排查用的扫描命令，会阻塞 Redis，根本不是拿锁的机制。
DEL 只是释放动作，它本身不创建任何租约，没法完成 hold。
optionExplanations_en: NX guarantees the key is only created when nobody holds it, and EX guarantees it cleans itself up if the holder disappears—both options are essential.
A GET followed by an unconditional SET leaves a gap where someone else can still grab the key first.
KEYS * is a debugging scan that can block Redis; it isn't a locking mechanism at all.
DEL is only a release action—it never creates a lease, so it can't implement the hold by itself.

scenario: 用 `SET lock:A15 owner NX EX 30` 保护座位，但 worker 可能因 GC pause 卡住 40 秒。
q: Redis TTL lock 的经典风险是什么？
options: 持有者因 GC pause 或网络变慢而超过 TTL 后，锁被别人拿到，短时间内双方都以为自己持有这把锁
Redis 里设置的 TTL 数值在任何情况下都永远都不会真正失效或被自动清理掉
NX 选项会让所有并发到达的请求都在同一时刻各自写入成功，彼此之间完全互不阻挡也不会互相干扰，等于没有互斥
Redis 这种内存存储引擎本身完全不支持给任何 key 设置带存活时长的过期字段
options_en: If the holder stalls past the TTL due to a GC pause or slow network, someone else grabs the lock and briefly both sides think they hold it.
A TTL value set on a Redis key will never actually lapse or get cleaned up automatically under any circumstances.
The NX option lets every concurrent request succeed in writing at the very same instant with none of them blocking each other, giving no mutual exclusion at all.
Redis as an in-memory storage engine simply does not support setting any kind of lifetime field on any key at all.
codeSample:
# EX 30 = the lease; after 30s Redis hands seat A15 to someone else
SET lock:A15 owner123 NX EX 30
# the holder must carry a token the storage can compare on write
UPDATE seats SET status='sold', lock_token=42
 WHERE id='A15' AND lock_token <= 42;  -- a stale holder writes nothing
why: TTL 既自动清理死锁，也是租约边界：holder 超时后别人拿到锁，两方都以为自己持锁就是 double-grant。正确性最终靠 fencing token 或写入时的条件检查兜底。
why_en: A TTL both cleans up dead locks and caps the lease, so a stalled holder can overrun it and two owners believe they hold the lock — the real guard is a fencing token or a conditional write at commit time.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带有效期的临时持有权，到期后自动失效，不需要显式释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lease is a temporary right to hold something that automatically expires without needing an explicit release.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis SET 命令的选项，只有 key 不存在时才会写入成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NX is a Redis SET option that only writes the key if it does not already exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次发锁都带一个递增编号，存储只接受编号不小于已见最大值的写入，挡住过期持有者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is an increasing number handed out with each lock, and the storage rejects any write that carries an older token.

q_en: What is the classic risk of a Redis TTL lock?
optionExplanations: 持有者因为 GC 暂停或网络卡顿超过了租约时间，锁被下一个人拿到，短时间内两边都以为自己还持有锁。
TTL 到时候 key 确实会被清掉，这不是问题所在。
NX 的作用正相反，它只让第一个到达的请求成功创建 key。
Redis 原生就支持给 key 设置存活时长，这不是限制。
optionExplanations_en: If the holder stalls past its lease—say from a GC pause or slow network—the next requester grabs the lock, and briefly both sides think they hold it.
A TTL key does get cleaned up once its time is up; that isn't the problem here.
NX does the opposite—it only lets the first arriving request succeed in creating the key.
Redis natively supports setting a lifetime on a key; that isn't a real limitation.
scenario_en: You guard seat A15 with SET lock NX EX 30, but a worker can stall for forty seconds on a GC pause.

scenario: 你已经有 seats 表，想直接用数据库列实现 10 分钟 reservation，不想引入 Redis 这类额外组件。
q: 这段 SQL 的关键语义是什么？
options: 只有座位未被预订、或预订已经过期时才能抢到 hold；更新到 1 行代表成功
它会无条件覆盖任何人手上仍然有效的 reservation
它必须依赖一个后台清理 job 运行之后，过期的 hold 才会重新可用
它在语法上没有办法用来表达过期时间
options_en: The hold succeeds only if the seat is unreserved or the previous reservation has already expired; one row updated means success.
It unconditionally overwrites anyone else's still-valid reservation.
It depends on a background cleanup job running before an expired hold becomes available again.
It has no syntactic way to express an expiration time.
codeSample:
UPDATE seats
SET reserved_by = 'user123',
    reserved_until = NOW() + INTERVAL '10 minutes'
WHERE seat_id = 'A15'
  AND (reserved_until IS NULL OR reserved_until < NOW());
why: 过期逻辑写在 WHERE 里，所以旧 hold 到期后天然被视为空闲。优点是一致性贴近主数据，缺点是数据库写路径更热。
why_en: The database reservation succeeds only if the seat is free or the old hold has already expired.
tradeoff: 数据库列 reservation 的强一致和零新组件 vs Redis reservation 的更低写延迟
whenOtherWins: 高 QPS 的临时 hold 用 Redis 更快；需要强一致贴近核心数据时，数据库列更直接。

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 语句里限定哪些行会被影响的条件子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WHERE predicate is the condition clause that decides which rows a SQL statement affects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

q_en: What is the key meaning of this SQL?
scenario_en: You already have a seats table and want to implement a ten-minute reservation directly with database columns, without introducing Redis.
optionExplanations: 只有座位没人占，或者上一个 hold 已经过了 reserved_until，这条 UPDATE 才会真的改到那一行，改动 1 行就是抢到了。
WHERE 里明明写着判断 reserved_until，别人还有效的预订不会被这条语句碰到。
过期判断直接写在 WHERE 里，读到这一行时数据库自己就认得出旧 hold 已经失效，不用先等清理 job 跑过。
reserved_until < NOW() 这种比较正是在用 SQL 表达过期时间，写得出来。
optionExplanations_en: The UPDATE only actually changes the row if the seat is unheld or the previous reservation has already lapsed; one row changed means the hold succeeded.
The WHERE clause checks reserved_until directly, so someone else's still-valid reservation is never touched by this statement.
The lapsing check lives right in the WHERE clause, so the database recognizes a stale hold the moment it's read—no cleanup job has to run first.
A comparison like reserved_until < NOW() is exactly how SQL expresses a lapsed hold, so it clearly can be written.

scenario: 团队要给普通的座位 reservation 挑协调机制，正在考虑是否专门搭一套 ZooKeeper/etcd 集群。
q: 用 ZooKeeper/etcd 做分布式锁，相比 Redis 或数据库 reservation，特点是什么？（多选）
options: 提供更强的协调语义和更完善的故障处理能力
依赖共识协议（Raft/ZAB）在多个节点间维护一致性
运维复杂度更高，需要额外维护一套独立的协调集群
在任何场景下都一定比 Redis 实现起来更简单
options_en: They provide stronger coordination semantics and more thorough failure handling.
They rely on a consensus protocol (Raft or ZAB) to keep multiple nodes consistent.
They add operational complexity because you must run and maintain a separate coordination cluster.
They are guaranteed to be simpler to implement than Redis in every scenario.
why: ZooKeeper/etcd 是专门的协调服务，适合复杂故障场景，但引入新的运维面。不要为了普通 reservation 默认就上它们。
why_en: ZooKeeper and etcd provide robust coordination through consensus, but they add operational complexity you should not default to.
tradeoff: ZooKeeper/etcd 的强协调保证 vs Redis/数据库 reservation 的简单和低运维

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门的分布式协调服务，用 ZAB 共识协议维护一致性，用临时节点在客户端断开时自动清理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a purpose-built coordination service that uses the ZAB consensus protocol and ephemeral nodes that clean up automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门的分布式协调服务，用 Raft 共识协议维护一致性，常用于保存 leader、锁等元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a purpose-built coordination service that uses the Raft consensus protocol, often used to store leader or lock metadata.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个节点就同一个决定达成一致的算法，即使部分节点故障也能保持数据一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consensus protocol lets multiple nodes agree on the same decision even when some nodes fail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立于单个数据库事务存在的租约记录，谁持有、何时过期，任何服务器都能读到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a lease record that lives outside any single database transaction, so any server can see who holds it and when it expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

q_en: Compared with Redis or database reservations, what characterizes ZooKeeper or etcd locks?
optionExplanations: 它们提供的协调语义更完整，能处理临时节点断连、leader 选举这类更复杂的故障场景。
靠 Raft 或 ZAB 这类共识协议在多个节点间保持一致，即使部分节点挂了也能维持正确性。
要单独运维一套协调集群，这是它们比直接用 Redis/数据库多出来的成本。
维护一整套协调集群显然比调用现成的 Redis 命令更复杂，这个说法说反了。
optionExplanations_en: They offer more complete coordination semantics, handling harder failure cases like disconnects and leader elections.
They rely on a consensus protocol like Raft or ZAB to stay consistent across nodes even when some of them fail.
You have to run and operate a separate coordination cluster—that's the extra cost compared with just using Redis or the database.
Running a whole coordination cluster is clearly more work than calling an existing Redis command—this claim has it backwards.
scenario_en: The team is picking a coordination mechanism for ordinary seat reservations and is weighing whether to stand up a ZooKeeper or etcd cluster.

scenario: 订票架构里关系库和 NoSQL 并存，你要判断哪些并发控制语义能跨存储通用。
q: 下面这些跨存储的技术映射，哪些是正确的？（多选）
options: Conditional write 在不同存储里体现为：SQL WHERE、DynamoDB ConditionExpression、Redis SET NX
OCC 在不同接口里体现为：version column、HTTP ETag If-Match、etcd revision
Pessimistic locking 体现为：SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 或者进程内的 mutex
Serializable isolation 这种能力大多数 NoSQL 默认都完整支持
options_en: Conditional write shows up as SQL WHERE, DynamoDB's ConditionExpression, and Redis's SET NX.
OCC shows up as a version column, an HTTP ETag with If-Match, and etcd's revision number.
Pessimistic locking shows up as SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or an in-process mutex.
Most NoSQL stores fully support serializable isolation by default.
why: 这些都是同一并发控制思想在不同系统里的不同形态。Serializable 主要是关系数据库的能力，多数 NoSQL/分布式存储并不提供同等语义。
why_en: The same concurrency patterns appear under different names across SQL, DynamoDB, Redis, HTTP, and etcd.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 语句里限定哪些行会被影响的条件子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WHERE predicate is the condition clause that decides which rows a SQL statement affects.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 给写操作附加的条件表达式，只有条件满足时写入才会成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ConditionExpression is DynamoDB's way of making a write succeed only if a condition on the current item still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis SET 命令的选项，只有 key 不存在时才会写入成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NX is a Redis SET option that only writes the key if it does not already exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门递增的整数列，每次写入都会加一，用来检测这一行有没有被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version column is a dedicated integer that increments on every write so you can detect if a row changed underneath you.

termDefinitions.meaning: ETag 是资源当前版本的标识，If-Match 请求头让服务器只在 ETag 仍匹配时才处理写请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ETag identifies a resource's current version, and the If-Match header makes the server apply the write only if that ETag still matches.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门的分布式协调服务，用 Raft 共识协议维护一致性，常用于保存 leader、锁等元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a purpose-built coordination service that uses the Raft consensus protocol, often used to store leader or lock metadata.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务内对 SELECT 出的行加行级锁，直到提交前其他事务无法修改这些行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE takes a row-level lock inside a transaction so no other transaction can change those rows until you commit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

q_en: Which cross-store technical mappings are correct?
optionExplanations: 同一个 conditional write 思路，在 SQL 里是 WHERE，在 DynamoDB 里是 ConditionExpression，在 Redis 里是 SET NX。
OCC 的版本比较在关系库里是一列 version，在 HTTP 里是 ETag/If-Match，在 etcd 里是 revision 号。
悲观锁在数据库里是 SELECT FOR UPDATE，在单进程里就是普通的 mutex，思路是同一个先占后决策。
SERIALIZABLE 主要是关系数据库提供的能力，多数 NoSQL 并不默认给出这么强的隔离保证。
optionExplanations_en: The same conditional-write idea shows up as WHERE in SQL, ConditionExpression in DynamoDB, and SET NX in Redis.
OCC's version comparison shows up as a version column in a relational database, an ETag/If-Match over HTTP, and a revision number in etcd.
Pessimistic locking is SELECT FOR UPDATE in a database and an ordinary mutex within one process—same lock-then-decide idea either way.
SERIALIZABLE is mostly a relational-database capability; most NoSQL stores don't offer that strong an isolation guarantee by default.
scenario_en: Your booking architecture has a relational database and NoSQL stores side by side, and you need to know which concurrency semantics carry across.

q: 按从简单到复杂的思路，排列 contention 工具的选择顺序：
steps: 如果决策必须跨等待、外部调用或多个步骤，用 distributed lock/reservation
如果检查能写成当前行上的谓词，先用 conditional write
如果是 read-decide-write，高冲突用 pessimistic locking，低冲突用 OCC
如果 invariant 跨不同 row 且没有共享冲突，用 SERIALIZABLE 或把它物化到单行
why: 原则是用第一个能覆盖正确性的最简单工具。不要一开始就上外部分布式锁。
why_en: Choose the simplest tool that protects the gap, escalating from conditional writes to locks, OCC, serializable, and reservations.
tradeoff: 越靠前的工具越便宜、限制越多 vs 越靠后的工具越通用、成本和复杂度越高
diagram:
flowchart TD
  C[Conditional write]
  L[Short DB lock]
  O[Optimistic version]
  D[Distributed coordination]
  C --> L --> O --> D

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts will happen and takes a lock upfront before deciding.

q_en: Order the contention tools from simplest to most complex.

scenario: 你的规则是“只有订单还没取消，才能把它标记为 shipped”，检查条件就是同一行上的 status 谓词。
q: 对这条规则来说，最合适的起点是什么？
options: Conditional UPDATE，用 WHERE status != 'cancelled' 做守卫
先专门搭建一整套完全独立的 ZooKeeper 分布式协调集群，专门用来管理这一类状态变更逻辑，再接进主流程
把这条路径上所有相关的每一个事务都统一强制设成 SERIALIZABLE 最强隔离级别
用一把持有时间很长的 Redis 分布式锁把整条业务处理流程都紧紧包住
options_en: A conditional UPDATE guarded by WHERE status != 'cancelled'.
Stand up an entire, fully independent ZooKeeper coordination cluster dedicated to managing this one kind of status change, then wire it into the main flow.
Force every single related transaction on this path uniformly into the strongest SERIALIZABLE isolation.
Wrap this whole business flow tightly in one long-held Redis distributed lock.
why: 这是同一行谓词守卫，单条 conditional write 就是最简单的解法。锁和分布式协调都会带来不必要的额外复杂度。
why_en: A same-row status predicate is best handled by a simple conditional update, not heavier coordination.
tradeoff: 单条 conditional write 的低成本 vs 分布式协调/SERIALIZABLE 的高通用性和高成本
whenOtherWins: 如果 shipping 决策还要读多个表、调用库存服务或等待人工确认，就可能需要更强的协调机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WHERE predicate is the condition clause that decides which rows a SQL statement affects.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a purpose-built coordination service that uses the ZAB consensus protocol and ephemeral nodes that clean up automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.
