q_en: What is the best starting point for this rule?
scenario_en: The rule is that an order can be marked shipped only if it is not canceled, and the check is just a status predicate on the same row.
optionExplanations: 检查条件就是同一行的 status，一条 conditional UPDATE 就把检查和修改绑成一步，成本最低。
为了同一行的状态判断专门搭一套协调集群，代价远超这条规则需要的保护范围。
这不是跨行的不变量，用不着为它把所有相关事务都升到最贵的隔离级别。
这里判断毫秒级就能完成，用不着让一把锁横跨整个流程等着被占用。
optionExplanations_en: The check is just a status predicate on the same row, so one conditional UPDATE bundles the check and the write at minimal cost.
Standing up a whole coordination cluster for a single-row status check costs far more protection than this rule needs.
This isn't a cross-row invariant, so there's no reason to push every related transaction up to the priciest isolation level.
The decision here finishes in milliseconds, so there's no reason to hold a lock across the whole flow waiting on it.

scenario: 多个用户会高频抢同一个资源，冲突非常常见，而且这个决策需要先读多行、再在应用代码里判断。
q: 在这种高冲突、read-decide-write 的场景下，优先考虑哪种机制？
options: Pessimistic locking，提前拿锁排队处理
OCC，并接受所有人不断失败、不断重试
完全不做任何同步机制，靠客户端自己兜底
把这条路径的隔离级别调到最弱的 READ UNCOMMITTED
options_en: Pessimistic locking, taking the lock upfront and letting requests queue.
OCC, accepting that everyone keeps failing and retrying repeatedly.
No synchronization mechanism at all, relying on the client to sort it out.
Downgrade this path's isolation level to the weakest option, READ UNCOMMITTED.
why: 高冲突下，提前排队通常比让大量请求做完工作再失败重试更稳定。锁能让竞争有序发生。
why_en: High-contention read-decide-write paths usually favor pessimistic locking over repeated optimistic retries.
tradeoff: 锁排队的稳定吞吐 vs OCC 高冲突下的重试风暴
whenOtherWins: 如果冲突其实很少，OCC 能避免锁等待；如果需要跨用户等待，reservation 更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前假设一定会冲突，先拿锁再决策，阻止其他事务同时修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts will happen and takes a lock upfront before deciding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最弱的隔离级别，能读到其他事务尚未提交、随时可能回滚的改动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: READ UNCOMMITTED is the weakest isolation level, letting you see another transaction's uncommitted changes.

q_en: Which mechanism should you consider first in this high-contention read-decide-write case?
scenario_en: Many users frequently compete for the same resource, conflicts are common, and the decision requires reading several rows before application code can decide.
optionExplanations: 高冲突下提前拿锁排队，虽然多了等待，但每个请求按顺序稳定地跑完，不会出现大规模失败重试。
冲突本来就常见，OCC 的乐观重试会让大量请求先花时间读多行、判断，最后还是撞车重来，工作量被反复浪费。
读多行再判断这一步天然有竞态窗口，完全不同步会让并发请求各自做出互相冲突的决定。
隔离级别调弱只会让更多冲突检测不到，跟解决高冲突问题的方向相反。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the lock upfront under high contention adds waiting, but every request then runs to completion in order, with no mass fail-and-retry storm.
Since conflicts are already common, OCC's optimistic retries let many requests read multiple rows and decide, only to collide and redo the work repeatedly.
Reading several rows before deciding leaves a real race window, and no synchronization lets concurrent requests reach conflicting decisions.
Weakening isolation only makes more conflicts undetectable—the opposite direction from solving a high-contention problem.

scenario: 面试白板上给了你一串功能，你要在几秒内点出哪些写路径需要显式协调机制。
q: 面试里遇到哪些场景，应该主动识别为 contention 风险并提出协调机制？（多选）
options: 多人抢同一份有限资源，比如票、库存、司机或拍卖品
需要防止 double booking 或 double charging 这类重复动作
高并发场景下更新账户余额、库存数量或协作文档
单用户本地的偏好设置，且完全没有其他人共享这份数据
options_en: Many people competing for the same limited resource, such as tickets, inventory, drivers, or an auction item.
Needing to prevent double-booking or double-charging kinds of duplicate actions.
Updating an account balance, inventory count, or collaborative document under high concurrency.
A single user's local preference setting that no one else ever shares or touches.
why: 共享资源、并发写、强一致需求三者叠加，就是 contention 信号。单用户私有状态通常没有竞争，不要过度设计。
why_en: Contention signals include shared limited resources, double-booking risks, and concurrent writes to important shared state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个进程/请求同时争抢同一份资源或同一行数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contention means multiple processes compete for the same resource at the same time.

q_en: Which interview scenarios should you recognize as contention risks and coordinate explicitly?
optionExplanations: 多人抢同一份有限的东西，比如票、库存或某个司机，这是最直接的 contention 信号。
重复预订或重复扣款一旦发生就是钱或资源层面的实际损失，必须有机制去重。
余额、库存数量、协作文档这些共享状态一旦被并发改写，就需要并发控制来保护。
只有本人能看到、能改的私有设置，没有别人跟你抢，通常不需要为它设计协调机制。
optionExplanations_en: Many people competing for one limited thing—tickets, inventory, a driver—is the most direct contention signal.
A double-booking or double-charge is real money or resource lost once it happens, so it needs a deduplication mechanism.
Shared state like a balance, inventory count, or collaborative document needs concurrency control once it can be written concurrently.
A setting only you can see and change has no one racing you for it, so it usually needs no coordination design at all.
scenario_en: On the interview whiteboard you get a list of features and have seconds to call out which write paths need explicit coordination.

scenario: 在线拍卖场景里，多人同时对同一个 item 出价，出价只会单调上升，不会倒退。
q: 对这种拍卖出价场景，常见的并发控制选择是什么？
options: OCC，把当前 high bid 当作单调 version/guard，只接受基于预期状态且更高的出价
对这个 item 的每一次出价请求都无条件地直接覆盖掉之前系统里已经记录好的这个历史最高出价，谁最后到谁赢
每次只要有人出价，就要把整个数据库直接锁住长达整整 10 分钟之后才能处理完这一次
完全按照用户过去积累的历史消费偏好来随机决定这次要接受哪一次出价
options_en: OCC, using the current high bid as a monotonic version/guard and only accepting a higher bid based on the expected state.
Unconditionally overwrite whatever high bid the system had already recorded before, for every single incoming bid, so whoever arrives last wins.
Every single time someone bids, lock the entire database directly for a full, uninterrupted ten minutes before processing it.
Randomly decide which bid to accept this time based entirely on a user's accumulated past spending preferences.
why: 拍卖很适合 OCC：高价单调上升，业务值本身可以当 guard，输的一方重读当前最高价后再重新出价。
why_en: Auctions fit optimistic concurrency because the monotonically rising high bid is itself a natural version guard.
tradeoff: 复用单调业务值做 OCC 版本 vs 额外维护一个独立的 version 列
whenOtherWins: 如果最后几秒同一 item 极度火热，可能还需要额外队列串行化该 item 的出价。

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拍卖里当前最高出价，只会单调上升，可以直接当作乐观并发的版本值使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The high bid in an auction only moves upward, so it can double as the version value for optimistic concurrency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门递增的整数列，每次写入都会加一，用来检测这一行有没有被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version column is a dedicated integer that increments on every write so you can detect if a row changed underneath you.

q_en: What is the common concurrency-control choice for this auction bidding case?
scenario_en: In an online auction, many users bid on the same item at the same time, and bids only move upward.
optionExplanations: 出价只会单调上升，当前最高价本身就能当版本用，输的一方重读最新价再出一次就行，不用另建 version 列。
无条件覆盖意味着一个稍晚到达的低价请求也能把刚写进去的高价盖掉，拍卖直接失真。
为每一次出价都锁库十分钟，会让整场拍卖被压成极慢的排队，跟出价的实时性完全冲突。
拍卖要按出价高低公平决定谁赢，跟用户过去花了多少钱毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Bids only rise monotonically, so the current high bid itself can serve as the version—losers just reread the latest price and rebid, no extra column needed.
Overwriting unconditionally lets a slightly late, lower bid stomp on the high bid that was just written, corrupting the auction.
Locking the database for ten minutes on every single bid would crush the whole auction into a painfully slow queue, defeating real-time bidding.
An auction should be decided fairly by bid amount, which has nothing to do with a user's past spending.

scenario: 票务系统里用户选好座位后要填写支付信息，产品要求不能让用户填完支付才发现座位已经被抢走。
q: 最能同时改善这次体验又保证正确性的 contention 方案是什么？
options: 用户选座的瞬间就立即创建一个带 10 分钟 TTL 的临时座位 reservation
什么都不做，等支付完全完成之后再去检查这个座位是否还在场
所有座位统一只用一个总库存 counter 数字，完全不单独跟踪座位本身状态，选座只减总数
让用户去线下柜台人工确认座位，完全不做任何线上的并发控制机制
options_en: Create a ten-minute TTL temporary seat reservation the very instant the user selects the seat.
Do nothing and only check whether the seat is still there after payment is entirely complete.
Track only a single total-inventory counter for all seats without tracking any individual seat's own state, and selecting a seat only decrements the total.
Have the user confirm the seat in person at an offline counter, with no online concurrency control mechanism at all.
why: 临时 reservation 把竞争窗口缩短到选座的瞬间，避免用户花时间填支付后才失败。它同时是正确性和体验优化。
why_en: A short seat reservation shrinks the contention window and avoids checkout failures after payment entry.
tradeoff: 提前建 TTL reservation 的体验优势 vs 支付完成才检查的实现简单
whenOtherWins: 如果资源选择和提交都能在毫秒内完成，单事务 conditional write 或行锁可能已经足够。

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

q_en: Which contention pattern best improves this experience while preserving correctness?
scenario_en: In a ticketing system, users enter payment details after choosing seats, and the product requires that they not discover the seat was taken only after payment entry.
optionExplanations: 选座那一刻就建一个十分钟的临时占用，把竞争窗口收紧到选座瞬间，用户填支付信息时座位已经是稳的。
等付完款才检查，用户十分钟表白填了才发现座位没了，体验和正确性都没保住。
只跟踪总库存分不出具体座位，两个人依然可能同时选中同一个座位号。
让用户去线下柜台确认完全不是在线售票该有的规模化方案。
optionExplanations_en: Creating a ten-minute hold the instant the seat is selected shrinks the contention window to that moment, so the seat stays reserved through payment entry.
Checking only after payment means the user fills out ten minutes of forms only to find the seat gone—bad for both UX and correctness.
Tracking only the total counter can't distinguish specific seats, so two people can still both land on the same seat number.
Sending users to an in-person counter isn't a scalable approach for an online ticketing system at all.

scenario: 支付平台把账户拆到不同服务和分片上，一次转账要原子地动两个独立的 source of truth。
q: 银行/支付系统里，什么时候 contention 问题会升级成 distributed transaction 问题？
options: 当一次资金移动必须原子跨越多个服务或分片，各自拥有独立的 source of truth
当只是在同一个数据库里，更新两个账户各自对应的那一行数据本身而已
当这次操作只涉及读取账户当前余额本身，完全没有发生任何写入相关的真实动作行为，没有任何冲突
当用户只是修改自己的昵称这类和资金流转完全无关的普通个人资料信息
options_en: When one money movement must atomically span multiple services or shards, each with its own independent source of truth.
When it is just updating the two account rows themselves inside one and the same single database.
When the operation only involves reading the current balance itself with no actual write action of any kind occurring, and no conflict at all.
When a user is only editing their own display name, ordinary personal profile information entirely unrelated to any money movement.
why: 单库内的余额更新可用锁或 OCC 解决；一旦要跨服务/跨分片原子转账，就超出了 contention pattern，进入 distributed transaction 范畴。
why_en: Money movement becomes a distributed-transaction problem when it must atomically span multiple sources of truth.
tradeoff: 单库内 contention 工具（锁/OCC）能直接搞定 vs 跨库/跨服务需要 distributed transaction 协议

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次操作必须原子跨越多个数据库、分片或服务的场景，超出单一 source of truth 能处理的范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed transaction is when one operation must atomically span multiple databases, shards, or services.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某份数据被认为权威、正确性最终以它为准的那个存储位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the one place a piece of data is considered authoritative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁定特定行，而不是锁整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row lock protects a specific row instead of locking the whole table.

q_en: When does a bank or payment contention problem become a distributed transaction problem?
optionExplanations: 一次转账要同时改动分别属于不同服务或分片的账本，各自都是独立权威源，这就超出单库能保护的范围了。
两个账户行都在同一个数据库里，用行锁或 OCC 在本地事务内就能保证原子性，不用上分布式事务。
只读余额没有任何写入动作，根本不存在需要协调的并发冲突。
改昵称跟资金账本完全无关，不会牵扯到跨源的原子性问题。
optionExplanations_en: A transfer that must atomically touch ledgers owned by different services or shards, each its own source of truth, is beyond what one database can guarantee.
Both account rows live in the same database, so a row lock or OCC inside one local transaction is enough—no distributed transaction needed.
A read-only balance check has no write at all, so there's no concurrent conflict to coordinate.
Changing a nickname has nothing to do with the money ledger, so no cross-source atomicity problem is involved.
scenario_en: A payments platform splits accounts across services and shards, so one transfer must atomically touch two independent sources of truth.

scenario: 派单系统向某个司机发出请求后，10 秒内不希望同一个司机同时收到多个并发的派单请求。
q: 对这种短期占用场景，合适的做法是什么？
options: 把该司机状态设为 pending_request，并带上过期时间或 TTL
继续无差别地给同一个司机并发发出好几个派单请求来反复打扰他
只更新乘客侧的数据表，完全不改动司机那一侧相关的任何状态字段信息，司机仍算空闲
把所有司机的状态都永久锁住，一直到整个平台重启之后才能解除
options_en: Set that driver's status to pending_request with an expiration or TTL.
Keep sending several concurrent dispatch requests to that same driver indiscriminately, repeatedly bothering them.
Only update the rider-side data table and leave every driver-side state field untouched, so the driver still reads as idle.
Permanently lock every driver's status, only releasing it once the entire platform eventually restarts.
why: 临时状态 reservation 能阻止重复派单，超时后自动恢复可用。可以用 cache TTL 或数据库 status + expiration timestamp 实现。
why_en: A temporary pending-request status reserves the driver briefly and prevents simultaneous dispatches to the same person.
tradeoff: 带 TTL 的临时占用换取避免重复派单 vs 不加保护直接并发发请求的简单实现
whenOtherWins: 如果只是查询附近司机而不发起独占请求，不需要 reservation；真正抢占司机时才需要。

termDefinitions.meaning: 派单时给司机临时打上的占用状态，带过期时间防止重复派单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pending-request status is a temporary hold on a driver with an expiration so dispatch does not send it simultaneous requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

q_en: What is a good approach for this short-term claim scenario?
scenario_en: A dispatch system sends a request to one driver and does not want that driver to receive several concurrent dispatches during the next ten seconds.
optionExplanations: 给这个司机打上带过期时间的 pending 状态，十秒内别的派单请求会跳过他，超时自动恢复可派单。
同一个司机同时收到好几单派单请求，会让他不知道该接哪一个，体验很差。
只改乘客侧的表完全没有标记司机被占用，别的派单逻辑还是会把他当空闲司机。
永久锁住直到重启，意味着司机接完这一单后也没法再被派新单，池子会被冻结。
optionExplanations_en: Tag that driver with a pending status that lapses in ten seconds; other dispatch attempts skip them until it lapses and they become available again.
Sending the same driver several concurrent dispatch offers at once leaves them unsure which to accept—a poor experience.
Updating only the rider side never marks the driver as claimed, so other dispatch logic still treats them as free.
Locking permanently until a restart means the driver can't be dispatched again even after finishing this one—the whole pool would freeze up.

scenario: 秒杀开抢前 5 秒涌入百万请求，热门 SKU 只有 1000 件，且绝不允许超卖。
q: Flash sale / 秒杀库存系统常会组合使用哪些办法？（多选）
options: 库存扣减用 OCC 或者 conditional write 来保证正确性
购物车里的短期 hold 用带 TTL 的 reservation 改善体验
高峰时段用队列削峰、或者对热门 SKU 做串行化处理
完全不做任何库存检查，直接让所有请求都成交
options_en: Guard the inventory decrement with OCC or a conditional write for correctness.
Use a TTL reservation on cart holds to improve the checkout experience.
Absorb peak traffic with a queue, or serialize requests for especially hot SKUs.
Skip inventory checks entirely and let every request succeed.
why: 库存扣减是正确性路径，购物车 hold 是体验优化，队列能吸收尖峰。真实系统常常组合使用这几种机制。
why_en: Flash sales often combine guarded inventory updates, temporary cart holds, and queues for especially hot items.
tradeoff: 多机制组合覆盖正确性+体验+削峰 vs 单一机制实现简单但顾此失彼

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把针对同一资源的所有请求放进一个专属队列，由单个 worker 顺序处理，从根源上消除并发写冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue-based serialization funnels all requests for one resource through a single worker so writes never happen concurrently.

q_en: Which techniques are often combined in a flash-sale inventory system?
optionExplanations: 库存扣减用 OCC 或 conditional write 守住正确性，防止超卖。
购物车里的临时 hold 用 TTL reservation，避免用户填到最后一步才扑空。
高峰流量用队列先削峰、对最热门的那几个 SKU 单独串行化，避免全场被拖垮。
完全不检查库存直接放行，等于主动放弃正确性，秒杀系统不会这么做。
optionExplanations_en: Guard the inventory decrement with OCC or a conditional write to prevent overselling.
Use a TTL reservation for cart holds so users don't reach checkout only to find the item gone.
Absorb peak traffic with a queue first, and serialize just the hottest SKUs so they don't drag down everything else.
Skipping inventory checks entirely means deliberately giving up correctness, which a real flash-sale system wouldn't do.
scenario_en: A flash sale takes a million requests in the five seconds before it opens, with only a thousand units of the hot SKU and no overselling allowed.

scenario: Yelp 类系统里，多个用户几乎同时给同一家餐厅写 review，需要更新这家店的 avg_rating 和 review_count。
q: 针对这个聚合字段的并发写，合理的并发控制是什么？
options: 给 restaurant 这一行加一个专用 version 列，用 OCC 来更新平均分
无条件地直接覆盖 avg_rating，谁的写请求后到就以谁的结果为准
让所有餐厅共用同一把全局锁，串行化处理系统里所有餐厅的全部评论 review，吞吐被彻底压垮
只更新 review 明细表本身，完全不考虑聚合值最终是否还保持一致
options_en: Add a dedicated version column to the restaurant row and use OCC to update the average.
Unconditionally overwrite avg_rating directly, letting whichever write arrives last win.
Share one single global lock across every restaurant, serializing every review for every restaurant in the whole system, crushing throughput.
Only update the detailed review rows themselves, without considering whether the aggregate value ends up consistent at all.
why: 多条 review 并发更新同一个 business 的聚合值时，OCC 能检测出 stale 聚合并触发重试。专用 version 能避免 ABA。
why_en: Restaurant aggregate updates fit OCC with a dedicated version column that avoids stale rating writes.
tradeoff: OCC 只在真正冲突时才重试计算 vs 全局锁串行化每一条 review 的简单但昂贵
whenOtherWins: 如果评分聚合可以容忍延迟，异步流式聚合也能减少写路径上的 contention。

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门递增的整数列，每次写入都会加一，用来检测这一行有没有被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version column is a dedicated integer that increments on every write so you can detect if a row changed underneath you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个值从 A 变到 B 又变回 A，只做相等比较的版本检查会误以为期间什么都没发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ABA problem is when a value changes away and back, fooling an equality-based version check into thinking nothing happened.

q_en: What concurrency control makes sense for concurrent writes to this aggregate field?
scenario_en: In a Yelp-like system, several users may review the same restaurant almost simultaneously, and each review updates avg_rating and review_count.
optionExplanations: 给 restaurant 行加一个专用 version 列，写平均分时核对版本，撞车了就重读最新聚合值再算一次。
谁后到就以谁为准，会让先写入的那条评分贡献直接被吞掉，均分因此算错。
所有餐厅共用一把锁，意味着给 A 餐厅写评论也要等 B 餐厅的评论处理完，代价严重过头。
只写明细表不更新聚合值，读到的 avg_rating 会一直是旧的，跟实际评论对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Add a dedicated version column to the restaurant row and use OCC—reread the latest aggregate and recompute if the version has moved.
Letting the latest write win silently drops whatever the earlier review contributed, so the average ends up wrong.
One shared lock across every restaurant means writing a review for A has to wait on B's review processing—way more cost than needed.
Updating only the detail rows without the aggregate leaves avg_rating stale and out of sync with the actual reviews.

scenario: 面试里设计一个日活 10 万的预订系统，所有数据都在同一个 Postgres 里。
q: 面试里为什么不该一看到并发就直接上 Redis distributed lock？
options: 新组件会增加故障模式，很多场景用数据库事务、行锁或 OCC 已经足够解决
因为 Redis 这种存储引擎在设计上永远不能用来保存任何锁，只能做纯缓存
因为分布式锁在任何场景下都必然比条件写实现起来更简单
因为数据库这类系统天生完全没有能力处理并发写
options_en: A new component adds new failure modes, and many scenarios are already covered by a database transaction, row lock, or OCC.
Because Redis as a storage engine is inherently incapable of holding any kind of lock and can only be a pure cache.
Because a distributed lock is guaranteed to be simpler to implement than a conditional write in every scenario.
Because databases as a category of system are inherently incapable of handling concurrent writes.
why: 外部分布式锁是有成本的：可用性、TTL 语义、故障恢复、运维。先用 source of truth 能直接保证的简单机制。
why_en: Distributed locks add components and failure modes, so prefer database-native guards when they are already sufficient.

termDefinitions.meaning: 独立于单个数据库事务存在的租约记录，谁持有、何时过期，任何服务器都能读到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a lease record that lives outside any single database transaction, so any server can see who holds it and when it expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某份数据被认为权威、正确性最终以它为准的那个存储位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the one place a piece of data is considered authoritative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

q_en: Why should you not jump straight to a Redis distributed lock whenever you see concurrency?
optionExplanations: 多引入一个组件就多一种可能出故障的地方，很多场景里数据库自带的事务、行锁或 OCC 已经够用了。
Redis 完全可以拿来实现锁，这不是它做不到的事。
维护一整套分布式锁的可用性、续约、故障恢复，明显比一条 WHERE 谓词复杂得多。
数据库处理并发写正是它的核心能力，这个说法是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Every extra component is another thing that can fail, and a database transaction, row lock, or OCC is often already enough.
Redis can absolutely be used to implement a lock; that isn't something it's incapable of.
Keeping a distributed lock available, renewed, and recovering from failure is clearly more work than one WHERE predicate.
Handling concurrent writes is exactly what a database is built for; this claim is false.
scenario_en: In an interview you are designing a booking system with a hundred thousand daily users and all data in a single Postgres.

options_en: Call it out right there as a contention point and name the coordination mechanism you plan to guard it with.
Finish drawing the API and data model first, and only get into coordination mechanisms once the interviewer asks about concurrency.
Make a mental note and save it for the deep-dive section at the end, covering every concurrency issue in the system in one go.
Write down "use a distributed lock" in the requirements and defer which mechanism you actually pick to the implementation stage.
why: 判定强一致的那一刻就是 contention 信号出现的时刻，主动点出来才显示你看得见竞态；代价是要立刻给出机制选择，不能只喊问题名字。
why_en: The moment you write down a strong-consistency requirement is the moment to name the contention and the mechanism you will guard it with, rather than waiting to be asked.
tradeoff: 在需求阶段主动点出竞态并选机制 vs 等被问到再补，前者显示主动但要求你当场给出选型理由
whenOtherWins: 如果这条路径根本没有共享写（比如用户私有的偏好设置），不要为了表现主动而硬加协调机制。

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个请求在同一时刻争抢同一个资源，不加协调就会出现竞态和重复成交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contention is multiple processes competing for the same resource at the same time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里讨论一致性、延迟、可用性、规模这类系统属性的环节，而不是功能清单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements are the consistency, latency, availability and scale properties you pin down before designing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任何一次读都能看到最新已提交的写，不允许读到旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means every read sees the most recent committed write, never a stale value.

q_en: What is the highest-scoring next move at this point in the interview?
optionExplanations: 把「强一致」这条需求直接接上一句机制选择，是面试官判断你是否真会做取舍的地方。
等对方问就变成被动答题，而且到那时你的数据模型可能已按无竞争假设画好了。
攒到最后讲，前面画的接口和存储都没体现协调，deep dive 时要返工。
在需求阶段就锁死一个外部组件，跳过了「单库能不能扛住」这一步，正是常见的过度设计。
optionExplanations_en: Attaching a mechanism choice directly to the strong-consistency requirement is exactly where the interviewer judges your tradeoff reasoning.
Waiting to be asked turns it into reactive answering, and by then your data model may already assume no competition.
Saving it for the end leaves your earlier API and storage with no coordination in them, forcing rework during the deep dive.
Locking in an external component during requirements skips asking whether one database suffices, the classic over-engineering trap.
scenario_en: You are in the non-functional requirements step, you just decided that one ticket must never sell twice, and the interviewer has not raised concurrency yet.

scenario: 突然加场的演唱会让所有人同时写同一行库存，团队已经准备好上「单 worker 队列串行化」这套方案。
q: 在掏出队列串行化之前，应该先做哪一步？
options: 先问这个热点能不能被改掉：拆成多个等价资源，或把这类写降级成最终一致
先给这一行加读副本再做拆分，把打过来的写请求分摊到更多节点上，看还剩多少冲突
先把这条写路径的隔离级别提到 SERIALIZABLE，让数据库自己去中止那些互相冲突的事务
先搭一套专门的协调集群来发锁，它能扛住最复杂的故障场景，正确性上最没有后顾之忧
options_en: First ask whether the hot spot can be designed away: split it into several equivalent resources, or relax those writes to eventual consistency.
First add read replicas and split that row so the incoming writes spread across more nodes, then see how much conflict is left.
First raise this write path to SERIALIZABLE isolation and let the database abort the transactions that conflict with each other.
First stand up a dedicated coordination cluster to hand out locks, since it survives the nastiest failures and is safest for correctness.
why: 队列串行化给的是吞吐上限加一个单点，是最后手段；先改问题本身常常能让热点直接消失，代价是要动产品语义。
why_en: Queue serialization caps throughput and adds a single point of failure, so first ask whether the problem itself can change, which often removes the hot spot outright.
tradeoff: 改造问题本身（拆资源或放宽一致性）vs 保留单一热点资源再往上加协调基础设施
whenOtherWins: 当资源确实不可拆、又必须强一致，比如全场唯一一件孤品，改不动问题时才轮到队列串行化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 极高比例的请求集中打在同一个 key 或同一行上，导致该点成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot resource or hot partition is when a disproportionate share of requests concentrate on the same key or row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把针对同一资源的所有请求放进一个专属队列，由单个 worker 顺序处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue-based serialization funnels all requests for one resource through a single worker so writes never happen concurrently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许各副本短暂不一致，只要没有新写入最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows replicas to disagree briefly as long as they converge once writes stop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库的只读副本，用来分摊读流量，写入仍然只能落在主库上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the primary that offloads reads but cannot accept writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

q_en: What should you try before reaching for queue-based serialization?
optionExplanations: 把一个热点拆成 N 个等价资源、或让这类写不再要求即时可见，是不加任何基础设施的解法。
副本分摊的是读，拆分切的是不同的行，大家抢的还是那一行，冲突一点没少。
它能捕获冲突，但在最热的路径上会变成大量中止和重做，正是最不该用它的场景。
这是直接跳到最重的一档基础设施，还要多养一套集群，热点本身并没有被处理掉。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting one hot spot into N equivalent resources, or dropping the immediacy requirement, solves it without adding any infrastructure.
Replicas spread reads and splitting separates different rows, but everyone still fights over the same row, so no conflict disappears.
It does catch conflicts, but on the hottest path it turns into constant aborts and redone work, which is where it fits worst.
That jumps straight to the heaviest infrastructure plus a cluster to operate, while the hot spot itself is untouched.
scenario_en: A surprise concert has everyone writing the same inventory row, and the team is already about to build single-worker queue serialization.

scenario: 名人账号被上百万用户同时关注，follower_count 这一行成了写热点；产品上没人会去核对这个数字的实时值。
q: 对这个热点写，最划算的处理方式是什么？
options: 改成最终一致：先记关注事件，异步聚合计数，用户感知不到这几秒延迟
维持同步强一致，用行锁把并发的关注请求一个个串起来，保证这个计数在任何时刻都精确
维持同步强一致，用 OCC 加一个版本列，让撞车的关注请求不停重试直到自己写进去为止
给 follower_count 这一行挂上一批读副本，把关注写分摊到副本上处理完再异步回传主库
options_en: Make it eventually consistent: record the follow event and aggregate the count asynchronously, since users never notice the few-second lag.
Keep it synchronously strong: use a row lock to serialize the concurrent follow requests so the count is exact at every instant.
Keep it synchronously strong: add a version column and OCC so colliding follow requests keep retrying until each one lands.
Attach a set of read replicas to the follower_count row so follows are handled on replicas and shipped back to the primary later.
why: 这个计数没有强一致的业务理由，放宽后热点写整个消失；代价是页面上的数字可能短暂偏低，产品必须接受这一点。
why_en: Nothing in the product needs this counter exact, so relaxing it to eventual consistency removes the hot write entirely at the price of a briefly stale number.
tradeoff: 计数任何时刻都精确 vs 放宽一致性绕开热点写换吞吐
whenOtherWins: 如果这个数字是账户余额或剩余库存这类用户会当场核对、错了要赔钱的值，就必须同步守住。

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许各副本短暂不一致，只要没有新写入最终会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows replicas to disagree briefly as long as they converge once writes stop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任何一次读都能看到最新已提交的写，不允许读到旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means every read sees the most recent committed write, never a stale value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 极高比例的请求集中打在同一个 key 或同一行上，导致该点成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot resource or hot partition is when a disproportionate share of requests concentrate on the same key or row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库的只读副本，用来分摊读流量，写入仍然只能落在主库上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the primary that offloads reads but cannot accept writes.

q_en: What is the cheapest way to handle this hot write?
optionExplanations: 关注数没有强一致的业务理由，异步聚合后这一行不再被同时写，热点自然消失。
串起来意味着所有关注请求排一条队，热点没消失，只是把冲突换成了等待。
在这种极高冲突下，重试的浪费会超过它省下的锁开销，越热越吃亏。
副本只承接读，写最终还是要回到主库那一行，分摊不了写压力。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing in the business needs this count exact, and once it is aggregated asynchronously the row is no longer written concurrently.
Serializing means every follow queues behind the last one, so the hot spot stays and conflict just turns into waiting.
At this conflict level the wasted retries cost more than the lock overhead they avoid, and it worsens as traffic grows.
Replicas only serve reads, and the write still has to land on that row in the primary, so they cannot spread write load.
scenario_en: Millions follow a celebrity at once and the follower_count row becomes a write hot spot, while no product surface needs that number exact in real time.

scenario: 扣库存走的是 read-modify-write，读到写之间的空档只有几毫秒；开抢时 1 万人同时打同一行。团队认为「窗口这么小，不值得加协调」。
q: 为什么「窗口小」不能当作不做协调的理由？
options: 窗口再小，1 万并发全落在同一行上就会被放大成大量真实冲突
窗口的实际长度其实和网络往返、内存访问速度都没有任何关系，谈论它的大小毫无意义
并发数一旦上去，数据库就会自动把 read-modify-write 这个循环合并成一次原子操作
冲突概率会随着并发数上升而下降，因为请求被摊到了更多的连接和更多的工作线程上
options_en: However small the window, ten thousand concurrent requests on one row amplify it into a large number of real conflicts.
The actual length of the window has nothing to do with network round trips or memory access speed, so its size is meaningless.
Once concurrency is high enough the database automatically collapses the read-modify-write cycle into a single atomic operation.
Conflict probability drops as concurrency rises, because the requests get spread over more connections and more worker threads.
why: 冲突数量取决于窗口 × 并发密度，而不是窗口本身；规模再往上还要跨多个节点协调，复杂度还会再涨一档。
why_en: The number of collisions scales with window times concurrency rather than the window alone, and growing further pushes you into coordinating across multiple nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读一个值、在应用里改它、再写回去的三步动作，读和写之间存在可被插入的空档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-modify-write is the read, change, write-back cycle whose gap between read and write lets another request slip in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个请求读到同一个旧值，各自写回，后写的那次悄悄覆盖了前一次的修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update is when two requests read the same value and both write back, so one silently overwrites the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个请求在同一时刻争抢同一个资源，不加协调就会出现竞态和重复成交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contention is multiple processes competing for the same resource at the same time.

q_en: Why is a tiny race window not a reason to skip coordination?
optionExplanations: 几毫秒的空档乘上每秒上万次尝试，落在同一行上的重叠就不再是小概率事件。
窗口在内存里是微秒级、跨网络是毫秒级，长度恰恰由这些因素决定。
数据库不会替你把应用里的读和写合成一步，那需要你自己写成一条条件语句。
并发越高、同时处在空档里的请求越多，撞车概率是上升而不是下降。
optionExplanations_en: A few milliseconds multiplied by ten thousand attempts per second on one row stops being a low-probability event.
The window is microseconds in memory and milliseconds over a network, and those factors are exactly what set its length.
The database will not fuse your application-side read and write into one step; you have to write it as a single conditional statement.
Higher concurrency means more requests sitting inside the gap at once, so collision probability rises rather than falls.
scenario_en: The inventory decrement is a read-modify-write whose gap is only milliseconds, ten thousand users hit the same row at open, and the team says the window is too small to bother.

scenario: 扣库存用一条 `UPDATE concerts SET available_seats = available_seats - 1 WHERE concert_id = ? AND available_seats > 0`，Bob 是并发里输的那一方。
q: Bob 这条语句以什么形式失败，取决于什么？
options: 取决于隔离级别：常见默认下静默匹配 0 行，严格级别下抛 serialization error
取决于这张表上有没有为条件列建索引：建了索引数据库就会直接报错，没有索引时才会静默地匹配 0 行
取决于当前的并发连接数：连接数超过阈值以后，数据库才会把这次失败升级成显式的错误
不取决于任何东西：所有数据库的所有配置下都固定是静默匹配 0 行，永远不会抛出错误
options_en: The isolation level decides it: at common defaults it silently matches zero rows, at strict levels it raises a serialization error instead.
Whether the table has an index decides it: with an index the database raises an error outright, and only without one does it silently match zero rows.
The current connection count decides it: only once concurrency passes a threshold does the database promote this failure into an error.
Nothing decides it: every database in every configuration silently matches zero rows here and never raises an error for this case.
why: 两种形状的结果都是一座一卖，变的是应用怎么接：匹配 0 行要自己查 affected rows，serialization error 要 catch 住再重试。
why_en: Either way it is one seat and one sale; what changes is your app code, which must either check affected rows or catch a serialization error and retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条 UPDATE 实际改动的行数，条件不成立时是 0 且不算错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Affected rows is how many rows an UPDATE actually changed, and zero is not an error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库判定两笔事务无法串行排序时抛出的错误，应用需要捕获并重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A serialization error is what the database raises when two transactions cannot be ordered serially, and the app must retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

q_en: What decides the shape of the failure Bob gets?
optionExplanations: 常见默认下 Bob 重新检查条件、发现不成立、改动 0 行；严格级别改成让他中止并重试。
索引影响的是这条语句走不走全表扫描，和失败的形式无关。
连接数决定的是排队多久，不会改变一条语句失败时的返回形状。
严格隔离级别下确实会抛错，所以应用不能只写一套零行分支。
optionExplanations_en: At common defaults Bob re-checks the predicate, finds it false, and changes zero rows; strict levels instead make him abort and retry.
An index only affects whether the statement scans the table, not the form the failure takes.
Connection count decides how long requests queue, not what a failing statement returns.
Strict isolation levels really do raise an error, so the application cannot assume only the zero-row branch exists.
scenario_en: The decrement runs as one conditional UPDATE with available_seats greater than zero in the WHERE clause, and Bob is the loser of the race.

scenario: 每个座位已拆成 seats 表里独立一行、条件写打在 A15 这一行的 status 上；concerts 表上原来的 available_seats 计数器还留着。
q: 拆行之后，这个计数器该被定位成什么？
options: 派生数据：要么按需从座位行算出来，要么当缓存在同一事务里一起减
仍然是正确性的唯一守卫：卖票必须先通过它的大于零检查，然后才允许去改那一行座位的状态
必须删掉：只要系统里还留着任何冗余计数，座位行上的那条条件写就会失去它的原子性保证
可以放到另一个事务里异步更新：它和座位行短暂对不上，并不影响座位不会被重复卖出这件事
options_en: Derived data: either compute it from the seat rows on demand, or keep it as a cache and decrement it inside the same transaction.
Still the only guard for correctness: a sale must pass its greater-than-zero check before it is allowed to flip that seat row status.
It must be deleted: as long as any redundant counter remains, the conditional write on the seat row loses its atomicity guarantee.
It can be updated asynchronously in another transaction, since a brief mismatch with the seat rows cannot cause a seat to sell twice.
why: 守卫已经搬到真正被争抢的座位行上，计数器不再决定正确性；但异步更新会让它长期漂移，所以要么现算要么同事务维护。
why_en: The guard now sits on the seat row that is actually contended, so the counter no longer decides correctness; keep it derived or update it in the same transaction so it cannot drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某份数据被认为权威、正确性最终以它为准的那个存储位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the one place a piece of data is considered authoritative.

q_en: After the split, what role does that counter now play?
optionExplanations: 正确性已由 A15 那一行的 status 条件写保证，计数器只剩「还剩几张」这个展示用途。
它只能回答「还有没有票」，回答不了「A15 还在不在」，早就不是守卫了。
留着它并不破坏座位行上的原子写，只是它不再承担正确性责任。
异步更新会让它和座位行长期偏差，展示出来的余票数会越飘越离谱。
optionExplanations_en: Correctness now comes from the conditional write on row A15 status, leaving the counter only a display job.
It can answer whether any ticket is left but not whether A15 specifically is left, so it stopped being the guard.
Keeping it does not break the atomic write on the seat row; it simply no longer carries correctness.
Updating it asynchronously lets it drift from the seat rows, so the availability you display grows steadily wrong.
scenario_en: Each seat now has its own row and the conditional write targets the status of row A15, while the old available_seats counter still sits on the concerts table.

scenario: 两条新路径：转账前要读账户余额比对当天累计限额；下单前要读多个商品的库存，再决定能不能凑成一个 bundle。
q: 这两条路径该归到哪一类、用什么保护？
options: 都是 read-decide-write，判断在应用里做，用 FOR UPDATE 锁住读到的行再写
都是条件写，把日限额规则和 bundle 组合规则整个塞进一条 UPDATE 的 WHERE 谓词里就够了
都是跨行 write skew，两边写的行互不相交，只能靠 SERIALIZABLE 隔离级别去捕获这种冲突
都是跨服务的原子操作，属于 distributed transaction，应该按补偿流程而不是按锁来设计
options_en: Both are read-decide-write: the decision happens in application code, so lock the rows you read with FOR UPDATE and then write.
Both are conditional writes: push the daily-limit rule and the bundle-combination rule entirely into the WHERE predicate of one UPDATE.
Both are cross-row write skew where the written rows never overlap, so only SERIALIZABLE isolation can catch this kind of conflict.
Both are atomic operations spanning services, so they are distributed transactions and need compensation flows rather than locks.
why: 判断跑在应用代码里、写不进 WHERE，就必须把读到的行锁住扛过这段空档；代价是这些行上的其他写者要排队等你提交。
why_en: When the decision runs in application code and cannot be a predicate, you hold the rows you read across the gap, and everyone else writing those rows waits for your commit.
tradeoff: 锁住读到的行换取判断期间状态不变 vs 不加锁换吞吐但要承受 lost update
whenOtherWins: 如果判断能压回一条 WHERE 谓词（比如只比单笔金额上限），就撤掉锁改回条件写，别付不需要的锁。

termDefinitions.meaning: 读一批数据、在应用代码里做判断、再写回去；这个判断写不进 WHERE 谓词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-decide-write is reading rows, deciding in application code, then writing, where the decision cannot fit in a WHERE clause.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在事务里读的同时锁住这些行，别的事务要改它们必须等本事务提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE reads rows and locks them for the rest of the transaction so others must wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两笔事务各读一批重叠的行、各写自己那一行，单看都合法，合起来破坏了业务约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write skew is when two transactions read overlapping rows, each write their own row, and only together break an invariant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次操作必须原子地跨越多个服务或分片，各自拥有独立的 source of truth。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed transaction is one operation that must atomically span multiple services or shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个请求读到同一个旧值，各自写回，后写的那次悄悄覆盖了前一次的修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update is when two requests read the same value and both write back, so one silently overwrites the other.

q_en: Which category do these two paths fall into, and what protects them?
optionExplanations: 限额比对和 bundle 凑单都要先把数据取回应用里算，算完再写，中间这段空档必须锁住。
日累计和多商品组合是应用逻辑，写不成数据库能在写入时求值的一个谓词。
write skew 的特征是两边写的行完全不相交；这里两边抢的就是同一批余额行和库存行。
只要这些账户和商品都在同一个库里，就还是单库 contention，用不上补偿流程。
optionExplanations_en: Both the limit check and the bundle assembly pull data into the app, compute, then write, and that gap has to be held still.
A running daily total and a multi-item combination are application logic, not a predicate the database can evaluate as it writes.
Write skew means the written rows never overlap, but here both requests fight over the same balance and stock rows.
As long as those accounts and items live in one database it is still single-database contention, so compensation flows are unnecessary.
scenario_en: Two new paths: read a balance and check it against a daily limit before moving money, and read stock across several items before claiming a bundle.

scenario: 商品详情编辑路径每天几百次写，只有少数管理员能改，两人同时改同一条一年碰不到几回。团队想统一用 FOR UPDATE。
q: 在这种低冲突路径上默认加行锁，真正的代价是什么？
options: 每一笔事务都付了取锁和排队的保险费，而其中绝大多数本来就不会撞车
行锁会让这次写入不再是原子的，于是低冲突场景下反而更容易出现 lost update 覆盖问题
行锁会连带把这张表上的普通读请求也一起阻塞掉，读多写少的路径会直接变得不可用
行锁在低冲突下会自动退化成 SERIALIZABLE，数据库从此开始跟踪这条路径上的读写依赖
options_en: Every transaction pays the premium of taking a lock and queueing, while the overwhelming majority were never going to collide.
Row locks make the write non-atomic, so under low conflict you actually become more likely to hit lost-update overwrites.
Row locks also block ordinary reads on the table, so a read-heavy, write-light path becomes effectively unusable.
Under low conflict row locks degrade into SERIALIZABLE, and the database starts tracking read-write dependencies on this path.
why: 悲观锁是为「冲突一定发生」买的保险，冲突稀少时保费全打水漂；这时 OCC 的偶尔重试更便宜，代价是要写重试分支。
why_en: Pessimistic locking is insurance against a collision that here almost never happens, so every transaction pays a premium for nothing while OCC plus a rare retry is cheaper.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在事务里读的同时锁住这些行，别的事务要改它们必须等本事务提交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE reads rows and locks them for the rest of the transaction so others must wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个请求读到同一个旧值，各自写回，后写的那次悄悄覆盖了前一次的修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update is when two requests read the same value and both write back, so one silently overwrites the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最强的隔离级别，保证结果等价于把所有事务逐个串行执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SERIALIZABLE is the strongest isolation level, guaranteeing the result matches some one-transaction-at-a-time order.

q_en: What does defaulting to row locks really cost on a low-conflict path?
optionExplanations: 锁的成本落在每一笔事务上，而收益只在真发生冲突的那极少数几笔上兑现。
锁只会加强原子性，不会削弱它，lost update 恰恰是不加保护时才出现的。
FOR UPDATE 挡的是并发修改，普通快照读并不会因此被挡住。
隔离级别是事务自己声明的，取一把行锁不会改变它。
optionExplanations_en: The cost lands on every transaction while the benefit only pays off on the rare few that truly collide.
Locking strengthens atomicity rather than weakening it, and lost updates are what happens without protection.
FOR UPDATE blocks concurrent modification, while ordinary snapshot reads still go through.
The isolation level is declared by the transaction itself, and taking a row lock does not change it.
scenario_en: The product description edit path takes a few hundred writes a day from a handful of admins who almost never touch the same row at once, yet the team wants FOR UPDATE everywhere.

scenario: 座位 hold 记在 ZooKeeper 的 ephemeral node 上。某台 web server 拿到 hold 之后进程被 OOM kill，没机会做任何释放动作。
q: 这个座位之后是怎么重新变得可买的？
options: 客户端会话在心跳断掉后超时，它建的 ephemeral node 自动消失，座位随即可见
节点会一直留在那里，直到有人手动删掉它，或者跑一个专门的清理任务把这些残留节点扫掉
ZooKeeper 会把这个节点转交给集群里另一台还活着的 web server，由它继续持有到业务超时
需要事先给这个节点单独配一个过期时长，到期之后 ZAB 协议才会把它从各个副本上删除掉
options_en: The client session times out once heartbeats stop, its ephemeral node disappears on its own, and the seat becomes visible again.
The node stays there until somebody deletes it by hand or a dedicated cleanup job sweeps these leftover nodes away.
ZooKeeper hands the node over to another live web server in the cluster, which keeps holding it until the business timeout.
You must configure an expiry duration on the node in advance, and only then does the ZAB protocol remove it from the replicas.
why: 进程死 → 心跳停 → session 超时 → ephemeral node 消失 → 座位释放，不需要清理任务；代价是要等满一个 session timeout，还要多养一套集群。
why_en: The process dies, heartbeats stop, the session times out, the ephemeral node vanishes and the seat frees itself, but you wait a full session timeout and you run a cluster to get it.
tradeoff: ephemeral node 的自动清理与强一致 vs 多维护一套协调集群的运维成本
whenOtherWins: 只是一个软性座位 hold 时，带过期时间的 reservation 行或缓存 key 更便宜，不值得为自动清理养集群。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[Session open: create ephemeral node] --> B[Seat held]
  B --> C[Process OOM-killed]
  C --> D[Heartbeats stop]
  D --> E[Session timeout]
  E --> F[Node auto-removed, seat free]

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 里绑定客户端会话的节点，会话一结束就自动消失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral node in ZooKeeper is tied to a client session and disappears automatically when that session ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: 协调服务在多久收不到客户端心跳后判定会话已死的等待时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session timeout is how long a coordination service waits without heartbeats before declaring the client session dead.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 用来在多个节点之间保持写入顺序一致的共识协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast is the consensus protocol ZooKeeper uses to keep writes consistently ordered across nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条数据或一把锁自动失效前能存活的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a piece of data or a lock stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

q_en: How does that seat become buyable again?
optionExplanations: 会话一死，绑在会话上的节点跟着消失，这正是它为崩溃进程提供的天然清理。
节点的存活绑在会话上而不是绑在人工操作上，不需要额外的清理作业。
崩溃的持有者不会被「接管」，它的持有权直接随会话一起失效。
这是缓存过期时间那一套的做法；ephemeral node 靠会话而不是靠预设时长来消失。
optionExplanations_en: When the session dies the node bound to it disappears too, which is exactly the natural cleanup it gives crashed processes.
The node lifetime is tied to the session rather than to a human action, so no extra sweep job is needed.
A crashed holder is not taken over; its hold simply expires along with its session.
That is how an expiring cache key works, whereas an ephemeral node vanishes with the session, not on a preset duration.
scenario_en: A seat hold is recorded as a ZooKeeper ephemeral node, and the web server holding it is OOM-killed with no chance to release anything.

scenario: restaurants 表由另一个团队拥有，你加不了新列，但改平均分时必须挡住 review_count 从 100 掉到 99 又回到 100 的往返。
q: 加不了版本列时，OCC 的退路是什么？
options: 把读到的每个字段都写进 WHERE，只有整行仍和读到的一模一样时写才生效
继续拿 review_count 做等值检查，只要写的时候它还等于 100，就说明这一行确实没有被人动过
把这条更新放进重试循环，连续两次读到相同的 review_count 就认为这中间没有发生过任何修改
改用最后更新时间戳来检查，即使两次写恰好落在同一个时钟刻度上也不会影响判断的结果
options_en: Put every field you read into the WHERE clause so the write only applies while the whole row still matches what you saw.
Keep using review_count as an equality check, since if it still equals 100 at write time nobody can have touched the row.
Wrap the update in a retry loop and treat two consecutive reads of the same review_count as proof nothing changed in between.
Switch to a last-updated timestamp check, which stays reliable even when two writes land on the very same clock tick.
why: 整行比对能抓住任何变化，包括等值检查看不见的往返；代价是 WHERE 变得又长又脆，任何无关字段被改都会让你白重试一次。
why_en: Matching the whole row catches any change including the round trip an equality check misses, at the cost of a long brittle WHERE clause and retries from unrelated edits.
tradeoff: 整行比对抓住一切变化 vs 专用递增 version 列更便宜且不会误报
whenOtherWins: 能加列时永远优先专用递增 version 列；有些库还直接暴露内置行版本（如 PostgreSQL 的 xmin）可以顶上。

termDefinitions.meaning: 值从 A 变成 B 又变回 A，只做等值比较的版本检查看不出中间发生过修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ABA problem is a value going from A to B back to A, so an equality version check cannot tell anything happened.

termDefinitions.meaning: 假设冲突很少发生，先不加锁执行，写入时用版本值检测这一行是否被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare and detects them at write time with a version check instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 每行自带的系统列，记录写入这一行版本的事务号，可当内置行版本使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: xmin is a PostgreSQL system column holding the transaction id that wrote the row version, usable as a built-in row version.

q_en: With no version column available, what is the OCC fallback?
optionExplanations: 整行都进条件，意味着任何字段被动过写都会匹配 0 行，那次往返也就藏不住了。
这正是被 ABA 击穿的那条路：值绕一圈回到 100，等值检查什么都看不见。
两次读之间同样存在空档，读两遍只是把窗口挪了个位置，并没有关掉它。
时间戳可用的前提是每次写都更新它、且时钟精度细到两次快速写不会撞同一个值。
optionExplanations_en: With the whole row in the predicate, any touched field makes the update match zero rows, so the round trip cannot hide.
That is exactly the path ABA breaks: the value loops back to 100 and an equality check sees nothing.
There is still a gap between the two reads, so reading twice moves the window rather than closing it.
A timestamp only works if every write touches it and the clock resolution is fine enough that two quick writes differ.
scenario_en: Another team owns the restaurants table so you cannot add a column, yet your average-rating update must catch review_count going 100 to 99 and back to 100.

scenario: 拍卖平台上一款稀有球鞋有 10 双完全相同的现货，现在只挂成一件拍品，几千人同时对同一行出价。
q: 怎么从结构上把这个热点拆掉？
options: 开 10 场独立拍卖，每双一行，争抢被摊到 10 个互不相干的资源上
保持一件拍品，给这一行挂上 10 个只读副本，把涌进来的出价请求分摊到这些副本上处理
保持一件拍品，把出价请求哈希切到 10 个分区各自结算，最后再把结果合并回这一行
保持一件拍品，把这条出价路径的隔离级别降到 READ UNCOMMITTED，以此减少事务之间的等待
options_en: Run ten separate auctions, one row per pair, so the competition spreads across ten independent resources.
Keep one listing and attach ten read-only replicas to that row so incoming bids are handled across those replicas.
Keep one listing but hash bids into ten partitions that settle independently, then merge the results back onto the row.
Keep one listing and drop this bidding path to READ UNCOMMITTED isolation to cut the waiting between transactions.
why: 库存本来就是 10 个等价单位，把它建模成 10 行后每行的争抢降到十分之一；代价是买家要在 10 场里挑一场，成交价也会分散。
why_en: The stock really is ten equivalent units, so modelling it as ten rows cuts contention per row tenfold, at the cost of buyers picking an auction and prices splitting.
tradeoff: 把一个热点拆成 N 个等价资源 vs 保留单一资源再往上加协调机制
whenOtherWins: 如果资源天生唯一（一件孤品、一个具体座位），拆不出等价副本，就只能回到锁、reservation 或队列串行化。

termDefinitions.meaning: 极高比例的请求集中打在同一个 key 或同一行上，导致该点成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot resource or hot partition is when a disproportionate share of requests concentrate on the same key or row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reservation is a temporary hold with an expiration that reserves a resource without keeping a database transaction lock open.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最弱的隔离级别，能读到别的事务还没提交的中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: READ UNCOMMITTED is the weakest isolation level, where you can read another transaction uncommitted changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主库的只读副本，用来分摊读流量，写入仍然只能落在主库上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the primary that offloads reads but cannot accept writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把针对同一资源的所有请求放进一个专属队列，由单个 worker 顺序处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue-based serialization funnels all requests for one resource through a single worker so writes never happen concurrently.

q_en: How do you structurally remove this hot spot?
optionExplanations: 10 双货本来就可以互换，拆成 10 行之后每一行只面对十分之一的出价者。
副本承接不了写，出价最终都要回到主库那一行，热点没被动过。
出价要比的是同一个当前最高价，切成 10 个分区各算各的，结算时对不齐。
降隔离级别只会让人读到未提交的中间价，冲突一点没少，还引入了脏读。
optionExplanations_en: The ten pairs are interchangeable already, so ten rows means each faces a tenth of the bidders.
Replicas cannot take writes, and every bid still lands on the primary row, so the hot spot is untouched.
Bids must compare against one current high bid, and ten independently settling partitions cannot be reconciled.
Weakening isolation only exposes uncommitted intermediate bids, so the conflicts remain and dirty reads are added.
scenario_en: An auction site has ten identical pairs of a rare sneaker in stock but lists them as one item, so thousands of bidders hit the same row.
